data.title: Sony's Mark Cerny Has Worked on "Big Chunks of RDNA 5" with AMD
data.author: ZenithExtreme
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PlayStation与AMD的合作及其技术前景

不同观点：
• basfo认为，当前所有游戏主机本质上都是PC，只是前端和商店不同，且随着Xbox开始开放，PlayStation可能也会跟随。
• phkahler建议直接引用相关文章，提供更多背景信息。
• DiabloD3指出，RDNA5并不在路线图上，接下来的重点是UDNA1，这是一种与CDNA融合的架构，尽管一些文章标题可能引起误解。
• whatever1提到，PS5相对于PS4 Pro的性能提升并不如以前世代明显，现在的图形改进需要更多的计算能力，或者游戏引擎变得过于臃肿。
• georgeecollins对Mark Cerny给予高度评价，并认为Sony作为一个公司，能够让一位美国出生的游戏开发者（工程师）担任重要职位，显示了其开放和尊重专业的态度。
• LorenDB认为，如果PlayStation的贡献足够好，RDNA4到RDNA5的改进可能和RDNA3到RDNA4一样显著，只要价格合理。
• erulabs对UDNA1的软件支持表示期待，希望AMD能在数据中心领域与Nvidia展开真正竞争，但也担心AMD如果再次在驱动和支持上出问题，可能会影响其声誉。
• monster_truck指出，AMD与Sony在FSR 3和FSR 4上的合作早有先例，特别是在BVH优化方面。
• brcmthrowaway提出谁是更好的计算机架构师，Mark Cerny还是Anand Shimpi，引发对两位技术专家的比较。
• lofaszvanitt质疑，当前PS世代游戏数量有限，新技术应用的前景如何。
• shmerl询问Sony何时会在PS上支持Vulkan。
• ZenithExtreme提到，AMD的下一代GPU可能内含PlayStation技术。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及对Mark Cerny个人的高度评价，以及他在技术领域的贡献和影响力。
• 对AMD未来架构UDNA1的期待与担忧，特别是在软件支持和市场竞争方面的潜在风险。
• 对PlayStation技术路线的分析，包括RDNA和UDNA的演进以及具体技术（如FSR和BVH优化）的应用。
• 关于游戏主机与PC趋同的讨论，以及对未来游戏引擎和图形技术发展的看法。

data.title: A Higgs-Bugson in the Linux Kernel
data.author: Ne02ptzero
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者在Linux内核中遇到的一种难以重现的“Higgs-bugson”问题，影响了处理公司交易数据的系统（Gord）。问题表现为文件复制操作偶尔会失败，出现“权限被拒绝”（-EACCES）的错误，尽管文件权限设置正确。经过调查，作者怀疑问题与NFS和Kerberos认证相关。在NFS使用Kerberos时，内核通过`rpc_gssd`守护进程获取用户凭证，但检查日志未发现凭证问题。为重现问题，作者进行了多种测试，包括生成大文件和创建内存文件系统，最终通过一个内存内虚拟文件系统成功重现并理解了问题根源，涉及Kerberos凭证和NFS交互的复杂性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"Higgs-Bugson"术语的讨论、NFS与Kerberos在系统中的使用问题、Linux内核质量的讨论以及对技术术语来源的考据。

不同观点：
• **Higgs-Bugson术语的合理性**：
   - **gnfargbl**：认为"Higgs-Bugson"这个术语不准确，因为Higgs粒子的发现困难源于其生产截面低、衰变特征难以分离等技术难题，而非不确定性或难以复现性。他将寻找Higgs粒子类比为在巨大玉米田中寻找特定类型的发光虫子，强调了技术挑战。
   - **protocolture**：喜欢"Higgs Bugson"这个术语，认为比将其称为"系统闹鬼"更好。
   - **sedatk**：指出"Higgs-Bugson"与"Heisenbug"实际上没有区别，并通过考据发现该术语起源于2010年StackOverflow上的一次提问，随后被博客和新闻引用，最终出现在维基百科上。他认为这个术语的流行源于一次随意的创造。

• **NFS与Kerberos的使用问题**：
   - **alexpotato**：引用一位CTO的话，将NFS比作毒品，初期看似很好，但最终带来很多问题，尤其是在Linux和Windows混合环境下使用NFS时。
   - **emmelaich**：描述了在使用Kerberos进行跨平台认证时遇到的复杂问题和奇怪行为，涉及Windows、Linux和Java应用的不同版本。
   - **vrnvu**：认为NFS与Kerberos结合使用是简单且经过实战考验的方案，但也提到因此出现了一些内核bug。
   - **nycerrrrrrrrrr**：质疑为何仍在使用NFSv3而非NFSv4。
   - **rurban**：建议避免在混合Linux/Windows环境中使用NFS，尤其是Windows环境，认为这是噩梦般的体验。

• **Linux内核质量的讨论**：
   - **mikeyg**：认为Linux内核在2020年代的发布质量有所下降，提到了数据损坏、WiFi固件问题、图形 artifact 和崩溃等问题，并怀疑是复杂性增加导致工程过程不堪重负。
   - **jwillp**：赞赏文章写得好，并对Nikhil解决bug表示感谢，认为这是积极的贡献。

补充讨论：
• **技术术语来源的考据**：
   - **sedatk**：详细追溯了"Higgs-Bugson"术语的起源，指出其缺乏严肃的学术背景，并认为StackOverflow删除相关内容是因为视其为"编造的东西"，这可能反映了社区和平台对内容质量的不同看法。

争议焦点：
• **Higgs-Bugson与Heisenbug的区别**：
   - 评论中对"Higgs-Bugson"是否与"Heisenbug"有实质区别存在争议。**sedatk**和**alienbaby**都提到Heisenbug，认为两者没有区别，而**protocolture**则显然喜欢并接受Higgs-Bugson这个新术语。

• **NFS与Kerberos的使用问题在不同环境中的可行性**：
   - 对于NFS和Kerberos在混合环境中的使用，一些评论如**alexpotato**和**rurban**持负面态度，认为这会带来很多问题，而**vrnvu**则认为这是经过实战考验的方案。

44447259.article_content:
A Higgs-bugson in the Linux Kernel
Jul 02, 2025 |
13 min read
Share on Facebook
Share on Twitter
Share on LinkedIn
By:
Nikhil Jha
We recently ran across a strange higgs-bugson that manifested itself in a critical system that stores and distributes the firm’s trading activity data, called Gord. (A
higgs-bugson
is a bug that is reported in practice but difficult to reproduce, named for the
Higgs boson
, a particle which was theorized in the 1960s but only found in 2013.) In this post I’ll walk you through the process I took to debug it. I tried to write down relevant details as they came up, so see if you can guess what the bug is while reading along.
Some useful background information about NFS with Kerberos
The NFS (“Network File System”) protocol is designed to access a regular POSIX filesystem over the network. The default security story of NFSv3, which is what we’re using here, is roughly “no security” on an untrusted network: the server only checks whether or not the client is connected from a ”privileged” port number (i.e. less than 1024). If the client says it’s connecting on behalf of a particular user, the server just trusts the client. What could go wrong?
The other security option for NFS is Kerberos. When used with NFS, Kerberos cryptographically verifies the identity of the user accessing the file.
What’s the bug?
Gord often does large file copies to ship data around. These copies would very rarely fail with
-EACCES (Permission denied)
despite the permissions being correctly set on the filesystem. Although retries were possible, it would be sad to lose progress copying these files. Also, strange errors in data storage are scary! It’s possible that spurious errors could indicate a larger issue.
There was no obvious pattern in these copies failing. Even identical jobs running simultaneously didn’t necessarily fail together. We did have one clue: if we switched Kerberos off in the dev environment (because the error sounded auth related), the copies never failed.
So, maybe something was wrong with the Kerberos credentials?
How does the kernel get your Kerberos credentials?
In a typical userspace program making use of Kerberos, libkrb5 will parse some environment variables or a config file to find the location of a Kerberos credentials cache. However, applications using NFS don’t need to link libkrb5 or otherwise know anything about Kerberos. They just do normal file I/O syscalls (open, read, write, etc) as if they were accessing a local filesystem. So what’s going on?
It turns out the kernel gets credentials via a root userspace daemon called
rpc_gssd
. When your application does its first I/O syscall to a file on NFS, the kernel writes to a file on a special mountpoint to communicate with
rpc_gssd
. (Fun fact: this mountpoint,
rpc_pipefs
, is an entirely separate filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel, just like
ext4
or
nfs
itself.)
Making some simplifications, the rpc_gssd program grabs the user’s credentials, constructs the right Kerberos service ticket, and writes to the rpc_pipefs again with the result. This involves an API called GSSAPI (“Generic Security Services API”), which you’ll see mentioned throughout this post.
Looking at the rpc_gssd logs around the time of the bug, I noticed that the kernel hadn’t requested credentials for a while. The most recently requested credential should also have been fresh for another few hours. So, this was a dead end.
Trying to reproduce the bug
I decided to try my luck by running a slow trickle of writes over the weekend. It seemed like the issue would be key-related somehow, so having a long-running process would force key expiry and plausibly reproduce the bug.
Checking back in on Monday, none of the dozen boxes I ran this on failed. This wasn’t too surprising, because the issue was pretty rare in production.
I then generated some large (~200GB) random files, put them on a test NFS mount, and started copying them to another test NFS mount in a loop on even more boxes. Once again, none of these copies failed.
At this point I was surprised I hadn’t seen the issue. To make sure I wasn’t just getting extremely unlucky, I decided to scale up the number of copies running in parallel.
I was worried about wasting bandwidth and impacting other users, so I thought a bit about how to make the test a bit more lightweight. One easy win would be to copy from a local disk to NFS instead of from NFS to NFS. However, I had already requested boxes with tiny disks. Fortunately, I had a cool trick in mind.
Writing a filesystem
I decided to create a filesystem that contains large random files, but fits entirely in memory on small test machines. Here’s the idea: Instead of storing actual file content, I’d use a noise function (or hash function) to generate consistent random bytes on demand.
This turns out to be fairly straightforward. There’s a Rust crate called
fuser
that provides a nicely typed implementation of FUSE (“Filesystem in USErspace”). Around 20 minutes lat

data.title: Conversations with a hit man
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 《The Atavist Magazine》的一篇文章讲述了退休的FBI特工Myron Fuller与雇佣杀手Larry Thompson在路易斯安那州监狱会面的故事。Fuller前往探访Thompson，最初是为了讨论一桩困扰他多年的谋杀案——Maria Marshall被雇凶杀害的案件。Thompson因多次雇佣杀人而被判长期监禁，他在会面中表现得十分友好，甚至有些热情。会面中，他们不仅讨论了Marshall的案件，还提到了其他案件。Fuller希望通过这次对话，能解开自己心理上的某些心结，因为当年在路易斯安那州任职期间，他未能阻止这起谋杀，这成为他职业生涯中的一大遗憾。文章描绘了两人之间的复杂关系以及这次特殊会面的场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一篇犯罪故事的评论，涉及对故事内容、真实性、法律问题及相关文章的讨论。

不同观点：
• [keiferski] 认为故事有趣且值得一读，特别适合对1960-1980年间美国南部犯罪与腐败感兴趣的读者。他将故事氛围与电视剧《True Detective》第一季相比较，指出两者都以路易斯安那州为背景。

• [crossroadsguy] 对故事中涉及的法律问题提出质疑，特别关注凶手与州政府达成"交易"的合法性和合理性，质疑法官在其中的作用，以及这种交易是否意味着凶手可以通过认罪获得大幅减少刑期。他引用了一篇文章来支持自己的疑问。

• [garaetjjte] 对故事中提到的一位杀手的可信度提出怀疑，认为该杀手的叙述可能是编造的，尤其是在其叙述与公开档案记录矛盾的情况下。他还指出，该杀手在其他案件中并未使用化名，但在文中所提案件中却使用了化名，这让人怀疑其真实性。

• [Communitivity] 表示故事唤起了自己的一些回忆，并提到自己曾关注过一个类似的旅行故事系列《She's a Flight Risk》。虽然有人认为该故事是骗局，但他表示自己并不完全相信这种说法，甚至希望故事中的角色能够在现实中过上自由的生活。

• [Neywiny] 认为故事写得不错，具有阅读价值，但不太确定该故事在这个网站上的具体角色或定位。

• [RickJWagner] 简单表达了对故事的赞赏，认为故事写得好且令人享受。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于故事中涉及的法律交易的合理性以及杀手叙述的真实性。
• [crossroadsguy] 和 [garaetjjte] 都对故事中的某些细节表示怀疑，但角度不同：前者关注法律和正义问题，后者质疑故事中关键人物的可信度。
• [Communitivity] 的评论引入了一个与故事可能相关的其他作品，并表达了对故事真实性的个人看法，显示出读者对故事的不同解读。

44434245.article_content:
Like what you’re reading?
Subscribe to
The Atavist Magazine
today for access to our full archive.
Conversations
with
a Hit Man
A former FBI agent traveled to Louisiana to ask a hired killer about a murder that haunted him. Then they started talking about a different case altogether.
By David Howard
The
Atavist
Magazine, No. 164
David Howard is a journalist and the author of
Chasing Phil: The Adventures of Two Undercover Agents with the World’s Most Charming Con Man
. He previously worked as an editor for
Backpacker
,
Bicycling
,
Popular Mechanics
,
and
Prevention
.
Editor:
Jonah Ogles
Art Director:
Ed Johnson
Copy Editor:
Sean Cooper
Fact Checker:
Kyla Jones
Illustrator:
Björn Griesbach
Published in June 2025.
1
The killer is happy
to see us. That’s the first thing we notice when we spot Larry Thompson halfway across the visitation room of the David Wade Correctional Center. He rises from a chair and waves, his face unfurling into an avuncular grin. Our separate journeys to this prison in Homer, Louisiana—me from Maine, and Myron Fuller from the mountains of Utah—afforded plenty of time to set expectations, and neither of us anticipated a Norman Rockwell greeting. I pictured a menacing scene bathed in the neo-noir lighting of
The Silence of the Lambs.
And Fuller? He long believed that the next time he and Thompson saw each other would be through gun sights.
The visitation room Warden Jerry Goodwin escorted us into is large, square, and filled with cafeteria-style tables. It’s December 2021. Lights on a small artificial Christmas tree wink, at once cheery and monstrously sad. Vending machines line one wall, glowing sentinels filled with bags of junk food. During normal visiting hours, the chatter of reunited families animates the room. But Fuller is a retired FBI agent with an illustrious career, I’m an experienced journalist, and Thompson is a model inmate, his vast criminal history notwithstanding. As such, Goodwin has granted us special privileges: an open-ended block of time, and a dedicated room with no bars or glass partitions, just a bored-looking guard at a nearby desk.
“Larry,” Fuller says.
“Good to see you,” Thompson drawls. The two old adversaries take chairs facing each other across six feet of wood laminate. I perch on a bench halfway between them and fan out the objects I’ve been permitted: notepad, pen, digital recorder.
At 78, Thompson is 18 years into an 80-year prison sentence for attempted first-degree murder and aggravated burglary. (A 35-year federal term theoretically begins after that.) One morning in 2003, Larry and his son Larry Neal Thompson Jr., along with four other men, robbed an Intertrust Armored Services car. They were spotted by a witness—a rare event in Thompson’s long criminal career—and a cop chased their escape van. One of the men shot an AK-47 through the officer’s window, wounding him. A massive manhunt ensued, and after several hours all six of the perpetrators were caught. They were subsequently convicted. Then, in 2014, Thompson confessed to four murders for hire in exchange for a reduced prison term for his son. (That deal never went through, because the official who overseeing it died before it could be finalized.) Thompson was later transferred to Wade from the maximum-security Louisiana State Penitentiary—better known as Angola.
Seated before us, he wears the standard-issue uniform: blue jeans and a light-blue chambray shirt. His hangdog blue eyes are framed by gaffer-taped tortoiseshell glasses that rest atop his prominent nose. His hands are missing parts of two fingers. “This one I cut off with an electric drill,” he’ll tell us later, holding up the stump of his left index finger. Then he’ll wave the remains of his right ring finger. “My dog bit me on this one.”
The warden tells us goodbye, then turns to Thompson. “Behave yourself,” he says, not unpleasantly. Goodwin hesitates for a beat, as if he wants to say something to us or is curious about why we’re here. Cops come to interview prisoners all the time, of course, but he doesn’t see many 79-year-old retired FBI agents dropping in on one of his more notorious inmates.
Fuller shakes Goodwin’s hand and thanks him. The truth, as best Fuller can grasp it himself, is that he’s hoping to dislodge a few ghosts from his psyche. He enjoyed an illustrious 31-year career in the bureau, with one notable exception: his tenure running the office in Shreveport, Louisiana, from 1981 to 1985.
What went wrong? Only everything. Crooked cops. Investigations that inexplicably faceplanted. Political interference. Wiseguys and one particularly ethically challenged attorney. And, most prominently, a murder Fuller believes he could have prevented: Maria Marshall, a mother of three. It was a hired job; her husband, saddled with debt, wanted to collect the life insurance. The hit man was Larry Thompson.

44434245.article_summary: 《The Atavist Magazine》的一篇文章讲述了退休的FBI特工Myron Fuller与雇佣杀手Larry Thompson在路易斯安那州监狱会面的故事。Fuller前往探访Thompson，最初是为了讨论一桩困扰他多年的谋杀案——Maria Marshall被雇凶杀害的案件。Thompson因多次雇佣杀人而被判长期监禁，他在会面中表现得十分友好，甚至有些热情。会面中，他们不仅讨论了Marshall的案件，还提到了其他案件。Fuller希望通过这次对话，能解开自己心理上的某些心结，因为当年在路易斯安那州任职期间，他未能阻止这起谋杀，这成为他职业生涯中的一大遗憾。文章描绘了两人之间的复杂关系以及这次特殊会面的场景。

data.title: Where is my von Braun wheel?
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了为何NASA在1962年放弃了旋转轮形空间站的研发，转而专注于阿波罗登月计划，导致人工重力空间站的设想被搁置。文章指出，这一历史性决策导致了之后长达半个世纪的小型零重力空间站的模式，给宇航员带来肌肉萎缩、骨质流失和视力问题等健康挑战。早期太空先驱如冯·布劳恩曾认为人工重力对长期太空生活至关重要，其设计的旋转轮形空间站本可实现这一目标。然而，建造大型旋转空间站面临工程挑战，需要解决如何将巨大结构装入细长火箭的难题。文章最后提到，商业航天公司如今重新考虑人工重力站的可能性，或能纠正这一历史性偏差，推动人类成为太空文明。

44455022.article_content:
Where is my von Braun wheel?
Completion: 95%
3604 words
Essay first planted: March 25, 2025 • Last updated: July 3, 2025
In 1962. There — that answers the clickbaity title right away.
NASA had viable designs for rotating wheel space stations that could have given astronauts artificial gravity. Then, the Apollo program effectively killed them.
While NASA’s lunar focus delivered the historic moonshot, it dismantled a promising engineering effort at Langley Research Center that might have revolutionized human spaceflight. That decision set us on a half-century trajectory of small, zero-gravity stations that continue to plague astronauts with
muscle atrophy
,
bone loss
, and
vision problems
.
Had NASA maintained its parallel pursuit of artificial gravity, we might now have permanent orbital settlements supporting deep space missions rather than the limited outposts we’ve settled for. This historical pivot point matters today as commercial space companies contemplate artificial gravity again, potentially correcting a costly detour in humanity’s path to becoming a spacefaring civilisation.
James Webb, the former NASA administrator immortalised by the JWST, standing underneath a prototype of a von Braun Wheel
The need for artificial gravity
Early space visionaries, such as Werner von Braun, strongly believed that settling the solar system required developing technologies to generate artificial gravity within orbiting habitats as — rephrasing
Heinlein
— space is a harsh mistress. Modern-day astronauts
exercise a few hours each day
to overcome
microgravity
’s effects on
the body
. Von Braun was convinced that rotating wheel space stations prevented such physiological problems and were thus “
as inevitable as the rising sun
”. In these systems, humans live along the periphery of a wheel, within which they experience gravity due to the wheel’s rotation. Popularised by von Braun in his 1949 sci-fi novel,
Project Mars
, and the
1956 Disney piece
, the concept actually traces back to
Herman Potočnik
’s 1929 book
The Problem of Space Travel
. Its legacy is perhaps why many felt that an operational spinning station was, at best, a couple decades away.
Enjoying this article? Subscribe to stay updated
Don't fill this out:
Sign up
I am also on X
@angadhn
and
Bluesky
.
Potočnik’s first conceptualised the rotating space station.
von Braun explaining the layout of his wheel-shaped station
The difficulty of building large stations
⊕
Rotational forces applied to wine tasting.
This elegant solution to generate artificial gravity, however, comes with a major engineering challenge. Much like a ferris wheel, the wheel’s rotation could disorient astronauts if spun too fast. If the wheel spins slowly then its physics dictates it must be quite large. For example, one of von Braun’s designs called for a massive 75 metre diameter wheel that generated lunar gravity if spun at 3 rpm and Earth-like gravity at 5 rpm — this range is considered
reasonable for astronauts
.
However, the physics of rockets presents a different obstacle as it must be slender, like an arrow, to escape Earth’s gravity well and reach orbit. This defines the main upstream engineering challenge: how can we fit enormous space structures into slender rockets? For context, even Starship’s
upper-stage
, which is about 9 metres wide and 22 metres tall cannot fit von Braun’s conceptual station in a straightforward manner.
Architects of the International Space Station (ISS), the largest space structure ever built, tackled a similar packing problem using multiple smaller spacecraft which connect, like space Ikea, into a structure greater than its parts. Such in-space assembly involves spacecraft either gently crashing into each other at specific connection points (a manoeuvre called
rendezvous and docking
) as well as
astronauts and space cranes
supporting finer assembly tasks. While this works great in theory, the ISS’s assembly needed over 40 rocket launches spanning several years (and even more launches for cargo resupply and repairs). More damning is the typical ISS crew size of 7, which is a little over twice that of the first ever space station, Salyut, from 1972. Clearly 50 years of space station development does not indicate that such modular in-orbit assembly will scale to von Braun’s
anticipated 80 humans
or, more relevant today, Starship’s
100
any time soon. Civilisation-scale megastructures like the Stanford Torus and O’Neill cylinders appear even more outlandish to discuss today than when they were first proposed in the 70s.
The Stanford Torus concept for 10,000 space settlers was proposed during the 1975 NASA Summer Study.
The O’Neill cylinder was proposed in 1976 by Gerard O’Neill.
From this vantage point, it is quite clear that the architectural bottleneck is a technology running through all operational space stations so far: their use of small ‘tin can’ modular spacecraft as the centrepiece for assembly, which is a legacy of Apollo. This, in my opinion, is unfit

data.title: AI for Scientific Search
data.author: omarsar
data.article_summary: 文章《AI4Research: A Survey of Artificial Intelligence for Scientific Research》综述了人工智能（AI）在科学研究中的应用。近年来，大型语言模型（如OpenAI-o1和DeepSeek-R1）在逻辑推理和实验编码等复杂领域展现了卓越能力，推动了AI在科研创新过程中的应用研究。然而，目前尚缺乏对AI4Research的全面综述。为此，作者提出了系统分类法，归纳了五大主要任务，识别了研究空白，并提出了未来方向，如自动化实验的严谨性和可扩展性。此外，文章还汇集了多学科应用、数据集和工具资源，以促进AI4Research领域的发展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在科学研究中的应用及其工具开发

不同观点：
• [工具需求与实现] gavinray 希望有一个能够自动化查找、下载相关论文，并生成概述和实体关系图的工具。他提到了一个名为Minicule的工具，但认为其功能侧重于概念提取，而非综合总结。fabmilo则推荐使用Zotero，并提到正在通过Gemini和Claude进行集成开发，尽管过程有些笨重。

• [对LLM的看法] Amaury-El 认为AI在科学研究中的应用令人印象深刻，但同时也担心人们会变得依赖AI，削弱人类自身的判断力和直觉。bossyTeacher 强调AI不等同于LLM，并预测LLM被淘汰后AI可能会面临品牌危机，提醒人们AI的定义在不断变化。

• [对文章内容的解读] mixedmath 指出文章实际上是一项调查，并引用了结论部分，强调AI在科学研究中的潜力以及当前知识的整合不足。他个人对数学领域的有效搜索工具有所抱怨，因此对这类调查感兴趣。

• [对文章来源的质疑] rob_c 对文章作者的隶属单位表示关注，尤其对字节跳动在化学或材料研究方面的创新能力持怀疑态度。

• [期望与现实] scientific_ass 本期望看到一个可以试用的产品，虽然有些失望，但整体上并不感到不满。

• [实习机会] Raghavendra8008 关心是否存在相关的实习机会，但未得到具体回应。

• 工具开发的需求集中在高效的科研工作流上，尤其是自动化处理和总结大量文献的能力。
• 对LLM的应用存在一定争议，部分用户担心其可能导致人类思维能力的退化，另一部分用户则对AI和LLM的区别及其未来发展表示关注。
• 对科研文章的来源和权威性的质疑反映了学术界对跨领域研究的谨慎态度。
• 用户对AI在科研中的实际应用充满期待，但也存在对当前进展的不满足感。

Abstract:
Recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly in large language models (LLMs) such as OpenAI-o1 and DeepSeek-R1, have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in complex domains such as logical reasoning and experimental coding. Motivated by these advancements, numerous studies have explored the application of AI in the innovation process, particularly in the context of scientific research. These AI technologies primarily aim to develop systems that can autonomously conduct research processes across a wide range of scientific disciplines. Despite these significant strides, a comprehensive survey on AI for Research (AI4Research) remains absent, which hampers our understanding and impedes further development in this field. To address this gap, we present a comprehensive survey and offer a unified perspective on AI4Research. Specifically, the main contributions of our work are as follows: (1) Systematic taxonomy: We first introduce a systematic taxonomy to classify five mainstream tasks in AI4Research. (2) New frontiers: Then, we identify key research gaps and highlight promising future directions, focusing on the rigor and scalability of automated experiments, as well as the societal impact. (3) Abundant applications and resources: Finally, we compile a wealth of resources, including relevant multidisciplinary applications, data corpora, and tools. We hope our work will provide the research community with quick access to these resources and stimulate innovative breakthroughs in AI4Research.

44455950.article_summary: 文章《AI4Research: A Survey of Artificial Intelligence for Scientific Research》综述了人工智能（AI）在科学研究中的应用。近年来，大型语言模型（如OpenAI-o1和DeepSeek-R1）在逻辑推理和实验编码等复杂领域展现了卓越能力，推动了AI在科研创新过程中的应用研究。然而，目前尚缺乏对AI4Research的全面综述。为此，作者提出了系统分类法，归纳了五大主要任务，识别了研究空白，并提出了未来方向，如自动化实验的严谨性和可扩展性。此外，文章还汇集了多学科应用、数据集和工具资源，以促进AI4Research领域的发展。
44455950.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在科学研究中的应用及其工具开发

不同观点：
• [工具需求与实现] gavinray 希望有一个能够自动化查找、下载相关论文，并生成概述和实体关系图的工具。他提到了一个名为Minicule的工具，但认为其功能侧重于概念提取，而非综合总结。fabmilo则推荐使用Zotero，并提到正在通过Gemini和Claude进行集成开发，尽管过程有些笨重。

• [对LLM的看法] Amaury-El 认为AI在科学研究中的应用令人印象深刻，但同时也担心人们会变得依赖AI，削弱人类自身的判断力和直觉。bossyTeacher 强调AI不等同于LLM，并预测LLM被淘汰后AI可能会面临品牌危机，提醒人们AI的定义在不断变化。

• [对文章内容的解读] mixedmath 指出文章实际上是一项调查，并引用了结论部分，强调AI在科学研究中的潜力以及当前知识的整合不足。他个人对数学领域的有效搜索工具有所抱怨，因此对这类调查感兴趣。

• [对文章来源的质疑] rob_c 对文章作者的隶属单位表示关注，尤其对字节跳动在化学或材料研究方面的创新能力持怀疑态度。

• [期望与现实] scientific_ass 本期望看到一个可以试用的产品，虽然有些失望，但整体上并不感到不满。

• [实习机会] Raghavendra8008 关心是否存在相关的实习机会，但未得到具体回应。

补充讨论：
• 工具开发的需求集中在高效的科研工作流上，尤其是自动化处理和总结大量文献的能力。
• 对LLM的应用存在一定争议，部分用户担心其可能导致人类思维能力的退化，另一部分用户则对AI和LLM的区别及其未来发展表示关注。
• 对科研文章的来源和权威性的质疑反映了学术界对跨领域研究的谨慎态度。
• 用户对AI在科研中的实际应用充满期待，但也存在对当前进展的不满足感。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：铜缆与光纤在短距离传输中的速度与延迟比较

不同观点：
• MadVikingGod：认为短距离内铜缆直接连接两台设备会比光纤更快，因为光纤需要重新信号处理。但他也提出疑问，这种低延迟是否会因高错误率和重传需求而被抵消，并担心多GHz信号下铜缆可能像天线一样产生干扰和串扰问题。
• jerf：同意铜缆在低延迟方面优于光纤，但指出许多人可能误解为这是带宽优势。他强调这里的“更快”指的是延迟而非带宽。
• throw0101d：解释Arista公司专注于低延迟网络设备，其客户包括高频交易等金融行业。Arista在扩展到更多领域后，也在超大规模数据中心中受欢迎。
• mousethatroared：铜缆的“更快”实际上是因为铜缆中介质的折射率较低，尤其是在铜缆可以使用空气作为介质时，而光纤不能。
• nimos：认为光纤的优势不在于信号传播速度，而在于信号完整性。
• exabrial：指出铜质SFP直连电缆本质上类似于“交叉电缆”，没有介质转换，因此延迟较低。
• feitingen：补充说明在双轴电缆中，光速略快于光纤，但在此比较中影响不大。
• asdefghyk：总结铜缆在某些情况下确实比光纤更快。
• citizenpaul：强调短距离传输中，DAC（直连铜缆）因无需模拟数字转换，速度更快是众所周知的事实。

补充讨论：
• zokier：质疑5纳秒的延迟改善在哪些应用场景中具有显著意义。
• SomeHacker44：提出空心光纤可能比铜缆更快，即使考虑信号转换和重定时延迟。
• deepnotderp：认为在这些距离上，前向纠错（FEC）延迟比传播延迟更重要。
• vlovich123：指出铜缆的“更快”仅限于短距离，因PHY层增加的额外开销较小。但如果光学计算可行，光纤将更快且发热更少。
• pfdietz：提到空心芯微结构光纤（HC-MOFs）能提供接近真空光速的传播速度。
• luxuryballs：开玩笑地建议测试银质电缆。

争议焦点：
• 铜缆与光纤在短距离传输中的实际性能对比，尤其是在延迟、错误率和干扰等方面的权衡。
• 不同应用场景下，5纳秒的延迟差异是否具有实际意义。

data.title: Stalking the Statistically Improbable Restaurant with Data
data.author: nkurz
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了美国城市中“统计上 improbable”（不太可能存在）的餐厅现象，如在较小城市中发现的高品质异国餐厅，这些餐厅反映了当地社区的特色。作者通过Google Places API收集了340个美国城市的数据，分析城市人口与餐厅数量之间的关系。结果显示，大城市如纽约的餐厅数量明显多于小城市，但有些中小城市因其“创意经济”或大学城特性拥有更多餐厅。作者创建了一个假想的平均城市“New Springfield, California”，拥有305家餐厅，其中20%为快餐店，包括多个连锁品牌。文章指出，数据并不完美，但可以帮助理解餐厅分布的总体趋势和异常情况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同地区饮食文化的分类、多样性以及影响饮食多样性的因素

不同观点：
• [giantfrog] 认为，美国的“数据驱动”分析虽然有趣，但在“民族”食物的分类上存在偏差。例如，Glendale, CA被标记为“地中海餐厅最多的地方”，但实际多数餐厅是亚美尼亚或波斯餐厅，这些餐厅被错误地归类为“地中海”而非“中东”菜系。这种分类模糊了不同地域美食的独特性。

• [jfengel] 分享了Laurel, MD的西非餐厅情况，尤其是不同国家的Jollof饭的区别，突显了非洲多国美食在美国的存在感。尽管该镇以非裔美国人和中美洲人口闻名，但非洲移民的餐饮文化也十分显著。

• [lwansbrough] 提出，城市的NIMBY（Not In My Backyard）程度与饮食选择的多样性存在关联。越依赖汽车的城市，快餐比例越高，而对房产使用限制较少的城市如Houston，则有更多样化的餐饮选择。

• [dawnofdusk] 关注Google Maps的AI总结功能，并提出是否能通过API查询特定菜系的关键词。他举例自己本地的中亚餐厅，虽然分类不太明确，但AI总结能提供更精确的地域标签。

• [djoldman] 列举了Carrollton, Texas等城市中韩国餐厅的比例，表达了对这些城市韩式餐饮集中度的惊讶。

• [yupitsme123] 通过数据展示了美国某城市连锁快餐店的密度，暗示了快餐文化的主导地位，可能限制了其他类型餐饮的生存空间。

• [SV_BubbleTime] 分享了在Allentown PA吃到的优质泰国菜，尽管当地有许多泰国餐厅，但正宗程度可能被低估。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于美国餐饮文化的分类和标签问题，尤其是如何正确区分和定义“地中海”和“中东”等菜系。
- 讨论中还涉及了城市规划、房产政策以及交通方式对餐饮多样性的影响。
- 有人关注AI技术在餐饮分类和搜索中的潜力，认为这可能有助于更准确地识别和定位特定菜系的餐厅。
- 不同地区的美食多样性与移民文化的关系也是一个值得注意的讨论点。

Stalking the Statistically Improbable Restaurant… With Data!
Stalking the Statistically Improbable Restaurant… With Data!
July 3, 2025
Last summer, I wrote about the
statistically improbable restaurant
, the restaurant you wouldn’t expect to find in a small American city: the excellent Nepali food in Erie, PA and Akron, OH; a gem of a Gambian restaurant in Springfield, IL. Statistically improbable restaurants often tell you something about the communities they are based in: Erie and Akron have large Lhotshampa refugee populations, Nepali-speaking people who lived in Bhutan for years before being expelled from their county; Springfield has University of Illinois Springfield, which attracts lots of west African students, some of whom have settled in the area.
Fine food from The Gambia in Springfield, IL
The existence of the statistically improbable restaurant implies a statistically probable restaurant distribution: the mix of restaurants we’d expect to find in an “average” American city. Of course, once you dig into the idea of an “average” city, the absurdity of the concept becomes clear.
There are 343 cities in the US with populations of over 100,000 people, from 8.47 million in New York City to 100,128 in Sunrise, Florida (a small city in the Ft. Lauderdale, FL metro area). Within that set are global megacities like New York and LA, state capitols, college towns, towns growing explosively and those shrinking slowly.
I’ve retrieved data about the restaurants in 340 of these cities using the
Google Places API
. This is a giant database of geographic information from across the world – not only does it include information about restaurants, but about parks, churches, museums and other points of interest. The API was designed to make it easy to search by proximity – “return all restaurants within 2km of this point” – but it’s recently gained an “aggregate” attribute, which allows you to ask questions like “How many Mexican restaurants are there in Wichita Falls, Texas?”.
The API is not perfect. I tested my queries on my hometown of Pittsfield, MA and while it got some questions (the number of Dunkin’ Donuts) completely correct, it missed others entirely, failing to identify our two excellent Brazilian restaurants when I searched for that category. We’re going to proceed with the assumption that the data is imperfect, and sanity-check when we get surprising results.
For starters, we look to see whether there’s a relationship between the population of a city and the number of restaurants located within city limits. It seems obvious that New York City should have significantly more restaurants than Lincoln, Nebraska, and indeed, that’s true. When we look at the whole set of cities between 100k – 8 million, there’s a straightforward linear relationship between population and restaurants with a few interesting outliers: Houston has more restaurants than we might expect, Phoenix fewer than we’d anticipate for cities their size.
The data is messier as we look at smaller sets of cities. Looking at cities with populations over 250,000, lopping off the four largest US cities (New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Houston), a linear regression no longer fits as well. Some of the cities that are celebrated for their “creative economies” – Austin, San Francisco, Portland, Seattle, Nashville, Boston – have more restaurants than we might expect, while some less celebrated cities of comparable size – Fort Worth, Jacksonville, Indianapolis, El Paso, Oklahoma City – have fewer than we might expect.
Exploring the cities between 100,000 – 250,000, there’s still a clear relationship between population and the number of restaurants, but that relationship explains just more than half the data variance (R2=0.5333) Some of the cities that are especially restaurant-rich are relatively small capitol cities – Little Rock, AR; Providence, RI; Baton Rouge, LA; Tallahassee, FL – and college towns  – Knoxville, TN; Tempe, AZ. Some of the cities that have fewer restaurants than expected are close to larger cities – Cape Coral, FL is next to Fort Meyers; Yonkers, NY is next to New York City; Moreno Valley, CA may be overshadowed by Riverside and San Bernardino.
(These are rough guesses based on staring at scatterplots. I’ll want to try some regressions before positing that capitol cities have a higher than usual number of restaurants because lobbyists need to take legislators out to eat.)
With all this data, we can now imagine an “average” American city of 100,000 people. We’ll call our imagined city “New Springfield, California”. (California has 76 cities with 100,000 or more people, ahead of Texas with 42. There are three Springfields in our set of cities, and 5 cities that start with “New”.)
There are 305 restaurants in New Springfield.
61 (just over 20%) are fast food outlets, including:
9 Starbucks and 4 Dunkin’s
6 McDonalds, 3 Burger Kings and 3 Wendy’s
4 Taco Bells and 2 Chipotles
9 Subways
3 Dominos and 2.5 Chick-Fil-A’s

data.article_summary: Philip I. Thomas宣布将其创建的个人网站和新闻通讯工具Postcard开源。Postcard最初于2022年推出，帮助Thomas在没有社交媒体的情况下通过电子邮件与朋友保持联系，并持续在其个人网站上发布月度动态。尽管收入微薄，Thomas仍坚持维护该工具，因其看重可靠的工具。为了方便更多人使用和定制，Thomas将Postcard的源代码发布，并进行了修改以支持"Solo"模式，简化单站点部署。开源版本包含Dockerfile和render.yaml文件，便于快速部署到Render平台。Postcard的代码现已在GitHub上提供，欢迎开发者使用和贡献。

44456827.article_content:
2025-07-03
Postcard is now open source
Self-host a personal website + newsletter
Philip I. Thomas
In 2022, I launched
Postcard
as a personal website + newsletter. I had deleted social media, and
wanted a way to stay in touch with friends via email
. It powers my personal website,
philipithomas.com
, where
I've published monthly "What I'm up to" every month since
.
Postcard's launch was well-received
and thousands of people signed up. Today, many people continue to use and maintain their Postcard sites. Revenue is modest - I make dozens of dollars per month on it. But, I'm happy to maintain it because I believe
dependable tools matter
. Today, I still maintain Postcard and the hosted service runs on a
Mac Mini on my desk.
I've decided to release the source code for Postcard. I update the service only occasionally, several developers have asked to contribute, and I no longer expect meaningful revenue from the project. Open-sourcing it feels right.
In the age of vibe coding, I think it would be fun to give people a working app they can customize. Postcard is a fairly simple application, written in
Ruby on Rails
, that works with few dependencies. So, it should be easy to run and customize.
In order to open-source Postcard, I made some changes to the code. Most significant is that I rewrote the application to support a "Solo" mode for running one single site, which simplifies the hosting and deployment for most open-source users. The hosted  service runs in "Multiuser" mode to support multiple users, custom domains, payments, and other options. The codebase includes both modes on the same
main
branch.
Deployment is straightforward. A Dockerfile is included, and a
render.yaml
file lets you ship Postcard to
Render
with minimal setup.
Check it out, fork it, and let me know what you build:
github.com/contraptionco/postcard
Subscribe for free?
I write about crafting digital tools.
Philip I. Thomas

data.title: Pbf2sqlite: Reading OpenStreetMap into a SQLite Database
data.author: amadeuspagel
data.article_summary: **pbf2sqlite** 是一个命令行工具，用于将 OpenStreetMap 的 .osm.pbf 文件读取到 SQLite 数据库中。它支持多种选项，如添加 R*Tree 索引、地址表和图形表。基本使用方法为 `pbf2sqlite DATABASE [OPTION ...]`，例如 `pbf2sqlite test.db read country.osm.pbf` 会读取 `country.osm.pbf` 文件并将其数据存入 `test.db` 数据库中。该工具的代码遵循 GPL-3.0 许可协议，目前版本为 0.1，预计2025年6月发布。主要技术栈包括 C、Python、Shell 和 Makefile。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[使用SQLite处理OSM数据的可行性及其在地理信息系统（GIS）中的应用]

不同观点：
• [teruakohatu] 提问是否可以将该工具用于反向地理编码。这表明他对工具的潜在应用场景有兴趣，特别是在反向地理编码方面。

• [juliansimioni] 对该工具表示赞赏，并提到在Pelias地理编码器中已经大量使用OSM和SQLite。他们目前使用自制的pbf2json工具，但认为创建SQLite中间数据库可以更强大地处理OSM数据，暗示这对数据导入前的操作有益。

• [tjridesbikes] 表示对该工具的极大兴趣，提到他正在做城市自行车路线地图的志愿工作，使用OSM数据进行标注。他认为拥有包含所有Way标签的SQLite数据库会使工作变得更加容易，对工具的实用性表示感谢。

• [milliams] 提问SQLite是否具备GIS能力，如PostGIS为PostgreSQL提供的那样，还是仅仅将数据作为传统数据库基本类型存储。这反映了对SQLite在GIS应用中能力范围的关注。

补充讨论：
• [juliansimioni] 的评论还提供了他们当前使用Golang编写的pbf2json工具的链接（https://github.com/pelias/pbf2json），显示了现有解决方案及对SQLite进一步应用的期望。

• [tjridesbikes] 的评论展示了该工具在实际项目中的潜在应用，特别是对志愿者地图制作的实用性，强调了工具的便利性和实用价值。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于SQLite是否具备足够的GIS功能来处理复杂的OSM数据。这涉及到SQLite在GIS应用中的适用性问题，[milliams] 的提问指出了这一潜在问题，需要进一步澄清SQLite的能力范围。

总结来看，讨论围绕SQLite处理OSM数据的能力及其实际应用展开，涉及到反向地理编码、数据处理的便利性以及SQLite在GIS领域的功能限制等问题。

pbf2sqlite
A simple command line tool for reading OpenStreetMap .osm.pbf files into a SQLite database.
Usage:
pbf2sqlite DATABASE [OPTION ...]
Options:
read FILE    Reads FILE into the database
(.osm.pbf or .osm)
rtree        Add R*Tree indexes
addr         Add address tables
graph        Add graph table
The command
pbf2sqlite test.db read country.osm.pbf
reads the
OSM PBF
file
country.osm.pbf
and creates in the database
test.db
the tables.
The tables created are described in the
documentation
.
OSM data can be obtained from a provider such as
Geofabrik
.

data.title: Flounder Mode – Kevin Kelly on a different way to do great work
data.author: latentnumber
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了凯文·凯利（Kevin Kelly）的不同寻常的职业道路和工作方式。他没有追求创立一家独角兽公司，而是以“好莱坞风格”工作，参与各种创意项目。凯利曾是《全球概览》编辑，帮助创建了早期在线社区WELL，并联合创办了《连线》杂志。他撰写了多本书籍和文章，涉猎艺术、旅行、宗教、创意和人工智能等领域。凯利还参与了斯皮尔伯格电影《少数派报告》的未来学顾问工作，并启发《未来世界》中的“死亡时钟”概念。他组织精选的长距离徒步旅行，还从事雕塑、绘画和摄影等艺术活动。

凯利提倡长期思考，正在建造一座可持续一万年的时钟。他也是一位重生的基督徒，并与妻子育有三个孩子。他早期提出的“一千个真粉丝”理论推动了创作者经济的发展。

作者布里·沃尔夫森（Brie Wolfson）反思了自己的职业选择，受到凯利不拘一格的工作方式启发，认为在硅谷以外也可以通过多样化的项目实现影响力和职业价值。她分享了自己在谷歌和其他创业公司工作的经历，最终选择追求自己认为有趣和有意义的工作，而不是传统的职业晋升路径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对技术乐观态度的讨论，以及对凯文·凯利（Kevin Kelly）个人影响力的评价

不同观点：
• [正面评价]

Essay
Flounder Mode
Kevin Kelly on a different way to do great work
By
Brie Wolfson
June 2025
PHOTOS BY ANDRIA LO
Kevin Kelly isn’t known for one ‘big thing’
, and doesn’t aspire to be. He’s as intelligent, hard-working, ambitious, and prescient as history’s most iconic entrepreneurs—only without any interest in building a unicorn himself. Instead, in his words, he works “Hollywood style”—in a series of creative projects. What follows is a sampling of his life’s work.
Kelly was an editor for the
Whole Earth Catalog
in the early 1980s, helped start WELL, one of the first online communities, in 1985, and co-founded
WIRED
magazine in 1993. He’s written a dozen books and published hundreds of essays on topics from art to optimism, travel, religion, creativity, and AI (even before it was a thing). Kelly rode a bicycle across the United States in his 20s. He was Steven Spielberg’s ‘futurist advisor’ on
Minority Report
, and the inspiration behind the famous ‘Death Clock’ on
Futurama
, after the show’s creator Matt Groening caught wind of the Life Countdown Clock Kelly keeps on his computer desktop. He organizes tightly curated group walks across Asia and Europe, regularly covering ~100km in a week. He sculpts, draws, paints, and photographs. And he’s a longtime friend and collaborator of Stewart Brand (whose famous line, “Stay hungry, stay foolish,” Steve Jobs quoted in his iconic commencement address at Stanford).
To encourage long-term thinking, Kelly is helping build a clock into a mountain in western Texas that will tick for 10,000 years. Brian Eno and Jeff Bezos are active collaborators. He’s a born-again Christian. He’s been married to his wife, Gia-Miin, for 38 years, and they have three children together. He was pivotal to a fringe-turned-mainstream movement to identify and catalog every living species on earth (now owned and operated by Smithsonian). He was early to think and write about the quantified self, which gave rise to products like Fitbit, Strava, Apple Watch, Eight Sleep, and the Oura Ring. Kelly’s idea of “1,000 true fans” practically christened the creator economy with his 2008 insight that “if 1,000 people will pay you $100 per year, you can gross $100k—more than enough to live on for most.”
The people who become legendary in their interests never feel they have arrived.
Kevin Kelly
Naval Ravikant has called him a “modern-day Socrates,” Marc Andreessen has said that “everything Kevin Kelly writes is worth reading,” Eno called him “one of the most consistently provocative thinkers about technology and culture,” and Ray Kurzweil said that “Kevin Kelly understands the direction of technology better than almost anyone I know.”
Kelly’s Hollywood style of working has always resonated with me; it’s the way I aspire to work and largely have since starting my career. Yet now, 15 years in, I’ve become self-conscious about it. Working in Silicon Valley will convince you that starting a company with its sights on unicorn status is the only possible way to make an impact, and the only work worthy of an ambitious individual.
Kelly is a cheerful and enterprising repudiation of that path, and I didn’t get very long into my interview preparations to realize that I wasn’t only writing about a personal hero; I was seeking a way to make peace with my own professional choices. After a day together, I realized that my pilgrimage to meet the man in his element might also grant permission to others in our line of work who are interested in charting a different course to impact.
I started my career
at Google selling AdWords to small businesses, and finished my first quarter as the number three seller in North America. Professional opportunities immediately unfolded—early nods for management, trips to global offices to present my “best practices,” my face on slides next to impressive metrics, and attention from more senior leaders.
It’s hard to say why none of that seemed very interesting, but it didn’t. What I did like was starting a campaign to rename the conference rooms and helping my coworker launch his internal content series,
G-Chat with Charleton
, in which he would interview Google executives while sitting with them in a two-person snuggie. I had earned myself a ticket to the fast career track at one of the coolest companies in Silicon Valley, but climbing the corporate ladder just wasn’t for me.
So I spent the next 10 years chasing what seemed most fun. After 14 months at Google, my work bestie, Jenny, and I left Google together to give the startup thing a try. We went to a mobile gaming company where I learned to make my way around spreadsheets, play Magic: The Gathering, and cash in on a blockbuster ‘pet hotel’ game. Eighteen months later, it was a six-person startup that was known as “the black sheep of Y Combinator.” In my free time, I coached a JV high school soccer team, volunteered at Dandelion Chocolate (all that working on software made me want to make something with my hands), and finished writing

文章介绍了凯文·凯利（Kevin Kelly）的不同寻常的职业道路和工作方式。他没有追求创立一家独角兽公司，而是以“好莱坞风格”工作，参与各种创意项目。凯利曾是《全球概览》编辑，帮助创建了早期在线社区WELL，并联合创办了《连线》杂志。他撰写了多本书籍和文章，涉猎艺术、旅行、宗教、创意和人工智能等领域。凯利还参与了斯皮尔伯格电影《少数派报告》的未来学顾问工作，并启发《未来世界》中的“死亡时钟”概念。他组织精选的长距离徒步旅行，还从事雕塑、绘画和摄影等艺术活动。

凯利提倡长期思考，正在建造一座可持续一万年的时钟。他也是一位重生的基督徒，并与妻子育有三个孩子。他早期提出的“一千个真粉丝”理论推动了创作者经济的发展。

作者布里·沃尔夫森（Brie Wolfson）反思了自己的职业选择，受到凯利不拘一格的工作方式启发，认为在硅谷以外也可以通过多样化的项目实现影响力和职业价值。她分享了自己在谷歌和其他创业公司工作的经历，最终选择追求自己认为有趣和有意义的工作，而不是传统的职业晋升路径。

data.title: Caching is an abstraction, not an optimization
data.author: samuel246
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了缓存（caching）的本质，提出缓存更应被视为一种抽象工具，而非仅仅是性能优化手段。作者认为，传统上缓存被用来提升数据读取速度，避免每次都访问后端数据库或API，但这种观点并不全面。通过处理数据在对象存储、磁盘和内存间的移动，作者意识到缓存其实简化了软件设计，使得不同存储层次的管理更加清晰。文章还指出，缓存算法（如LRU、LFU）提供了干净的抽象边界，尽管这些算法有时看似复杂，但它们在实际系统中不可或缺，因为数据访问模式难以预测。最终，作者强调缓存作为抽象的成功之处在于其隐藏了底层细节，但在出问题时才显得显眼，因此不应低估其价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：缓存与软件简化及抽象的关系

不同观点：
• ckdot2：认为缓存可以带来好处，但不能简单地认为缓存简化了软件。引用经典名言“计算机科学中只有两件难事：缓存失效和命名”，指出缓存的复杂性。
• necovek：缓存引入了生命周期管理等复杂性，不能直接说缓存使事情变得简单。缓存可以在抽象接口的实现中局部化，但缓存本身不是抽象。
• armchairhacker：优化通常需要重新思考代码结构，从而使代码更易理解。例如缓存级别迫使分离不同访问频率的数据。抽象是隐藏细节，例如垃圾回收机制。
• klabb3：作者指的是缓存可以作为存储访问系统中的实现细节，而不是直接管理多个存储层。缓存并非系统功能必需品。
• charleshn：缓存在分布式系统中引入双模性和亚稳定性问题，如DynamoDB设计中考虑了这些问题。
• LudwigNagasena：缓存是一种优化，有时可以被抽象掉，例如CPU缓存或构建缓存，但在网页缓存中很难完全抽象。
• neuroelectron：认为这是语义上的争论，不愿参与。
• TristanDaCunha：对整个讨论感到困惑。
• dasil003：缓存只是保持数据副本，增加复杂性，不能简化系统，也不是抽象。
• zmj：在单写单读情况下，缓存问题较少，多写多读时问题更复杂。
• gmuslera：性能元素包含在抽象中，优化抽象设计时也需要考虑性能。
• Joker_vD：缓存可能有多个用户，优化时需考虑系统整体性能，而不是仅满足单一用户需求。
• taeric：缓存策略和物化视图都可以作为缓存和抽象的辅助工具。
• eigenform：硬件管理的缓存是抽象的典型例子，存储位置选择被抽象掉。
• pclmulqdq：更好的抽象使用也是一种优化。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于缓存是否简化了软件以及缓存是否属于一种抽象。
• 部分评论者认为缓存增加了复杂性，而非简化系统，且缓存本身不是抽象。
• 另一部分评论者指出，在特定情况下，缓存可以作为优化手段，并通过抽象隐藏细节。
• 分布式系统中的缓存问题如双模性和亚稳定性也被提出，作为缓存复杂性的例证。

44432506.article_content:
June 30, 2025
Caching is an Abstraction, not an Optimization
I've always been told that caching is a tool to make software faster. That, given some careful considerations to consistency, caching makes it so that when you want to read a given piece of data, you don't have to go all the way back to some backend database or API server or SSD and can instead just read from some faster location like memory for the same data. Caching is thus a tool to improve performance.
My feelings now are that that perspective on caching is wrong, or at least incomplete. Having worked on software recently chiefly concerned with moving data between object storage, disk, and memory, I think now caching is probably best understood as a tool for making software
simpler
.
Something that always struck me as weird is, how come we have all these pre-baked caching algorithms, LRU, LFU, and so on. It seems like for my application I should have a much more fine-grained understanding of how things should work. Why am I outsourcing the understanding of my data to a generic "policy?" If I fetch some data, it seems like I
know
whether I'll need that data again in the near future, so I should explicitly be telling the system whether or not to hold on to it, and for how long.
One good reason is that it's a clean abstraction boundary!
Coming to caching from the belief that "I will personally manage when my data needs to be stored in faster storage" rather than the "naïve" belief ("I will go to disk every time"), caching much more resembles an
abstraction
rather than an
optimization
.
Two programs could have similar behaviour but structured very differently, the difference being that one utilizes caching as an abstraction and one explicitly has the concept of different tiers of storage.
As an existence proof, if you look at the systems, databases, which have to carefully manage the dance between memory and disk, you'll find they work this way. The way a buffer pool works is that any time you try to read data you first pull it into memory if it's not already there. The way OS disk access works is that any data you read first gets pulled into the page cache (unless you're using direct IO).
(As an aside that calculus may change somewhat for many workloads, with ever faster SSDs and ever faster APIs for accessing them, but that’s a story for a different time.)
My takeaway from this is that it's a reminder that it's possible to come up with a design that works, and that satisfies the functional requirements of a system from the perspective of "having adequate fast access to the data it needs" that nonetheless could be designed more cleanly and having more separated concerns.
Of course there are downsides to this particular abstraction, classically the OS page cache and
fsync
causes a lot of problems via misuse. It raises the question of "are these concerns truly separate."
Whenever I heard about people understanding caching algorithms better and spending more time on caching algorithms, it often seemed to me like a misdirection. This isn't the problem you want to solve, the problem you want to solve is "I want my data in fast storage as often as possible," not "I want to game this system that is holding my data access hostage." It feels like an unholy manipulation of
implementation details
secondary to what I actually want to do.
But I think two things are true that make this belief incorrect:
Data access is sufficiently unpredictable in real-world workload that we are forced to rely on heuristics, and fitting of heuristics, that we have to do this in any remotely realistic system. The belief that I'm doing this to the exclusion of some smarter, bespoke data movement strategy is an illusion.
Caching is in fact,
such
a good abstraction, that it
merits
this kind of arcane study to make it function better in practice. Caching can not fail, it can only
be
failed.
Maybe it's the curse of very successful abstractions that they're invisible until they hurt you, which means it's easy to undervalue them and in cases like mine, not even realize they're abstractions in the first place.

• zmj：在单写单读情况下，缓存问题较少，多写多读时问题更复杂。
• gmuslera：性能元素包含在抽象中，优化抽象设计时也需要考虑性能。
• Joker_vD：缓存可能有多个用户，优化时需考虑系统整体性能，而不是仅满足单一用户需求。
• taeric：缓存策略和物化视图都可以作为缓存和抽象的辅助工具。
• eigenform：硬件管理的缓存是抽象的典型例子，存储位置选择被抽象掉。
• pclmulqdq：更好的抽象使用也是一种优化。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于缓存是否简化了软件以及缓存是否属于一种抽象。
• 部分评论者认为缓存增加了复杂性，而非简化系统，且缓存本身不是抽象。
• 另一部分评论者指出，在特定情况下，缓存可以作为优化手段，并通过抽象隐藏细节。
• 分布式系统中的缓存问题如双模性和亚稳定性也被提出，作为缓存复杂性的例证。

data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了计算机科学中的“书架问题”（或称“列表标记问题”），即如何在有序数据中有效插入新数据，以减少移动现有数据的成本。像图书馆书架一样，预留空位可以方便新书的插入。这个问题涉及大规模数据管理，如社交网络连接或人口统计。尽管该问题看似简单，但在算法上已有30年未有显著进展。最近，研究人员开发出一种新算法，接近理论上的最低移动成本，即log2n。该算法通过随机化和非均匀分布数据，打破了以往的限制，为大规模数据插入提供了更高效的解决方案。这一进展有望应用于以往因成本过高而无法使用的情境。

44432351.article_content:
Further Reading
Drop in at a library, and you’ll likely notice that most shelves aren’t full—librarians leave some empty space on each shelf. That way, when they get new books, they can slot them into place without having to move too many other books.
It’s a simple-enough idea, but one that arises in a host of settings in computer science that involve sorted data, such as an alphabetically ordered census repository, or a list of connections between members of a social network. In such situations, where the entries can number in the hundreds of billions, the strategic positioning of empty spaces takes on great significance.
“Problems are getting bigger and bigger as we get more and more data,” said Helen Xu, an assistant professor in the School of Computational Science and Engineering at the Georgia Institute of Technology (Georgia Tech) in Atlanta. “At these scales, it becomes important to efficiently manage how you add new entries.”
The bookshelf problem (which computer scientists call the “list labeling” problem) is one of the most basic topics in the field of data structures. “It’s the kind of problem you’d teach to freshman or sophomore undergraduates,” said Guy Blelloch, a professor of computer science at Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh.
Yet until recently, there was a wide gap between what computer scientists could achieve algorithmically and what they knew about the theoretical lower limit on how many books you should expect to have to move when a new book arrives. On the algorithmic side, “There was pretty much no progress for 30 years or more,” Blelloch said.
Now, researchers have come up with a new algorithm that comes close to that theoretical lower limit. Blelloch described it as “a very elegant result.”
The new approach will “hopefully open the door to new applications of list labeling in settings where it wasn’t useful before because the cost was infeasible,” said William Kuszmaul, an assistant professor of computer science at Carnegie Mellon University and one of the researchers who came up with the new algorithm.
The list labeling problem starts off with a bookshelf of size
n
, along with some upper limit—say, 75% or 90%—for how much of the bookshelf you’re allowed to fill. There’s some chosen ordering for books (say, alphabetical by author), and as books arrive, one by one, you choose spots for them that respect the ordering, moving other books as needed. To find book-placing algorithms that are robust under many different conditions, computer scientists imagine that the books are being sent by an adversary who knows the algorithm and is trying to force you to move as many books as possible. (In some versions of the problem, the adversary may also remove books.)
If you were to use the most naïve possible algorithm—the one that places each book as close as possible to the start of the bookshelf—then your adversary could force you to move every book you’ve placed so far, simply by sending you books that precede every book they’ve already sent. As the bookshelf fills up, the cost of accommodating new books becomes proportional to
n
.
In 1981, computer scientists came up with a much better algorithm, whose average cost for adding a new book is only about log
2
n
. This algorithm starts by dividing the bookshelf into two equal chunks; then it divides each of those chunks in half, and so on. For each different size scale, the algorithm sets a threshold for how full the chunks of that size are allowed to be, with small chunks allowed to be fuller than large chunks. Once the books start arriving, if a new book pushes some chunk over its density threshold, the algorithm spreads out the books in the next larger chunk so they are evenly spaced, easing the pressure on the smaller chunk.
In the years that followed, researchers came up with variations on the theme of spreading books out evenly—“smooth” algorithms, as they’re called. However, no one could beat the log
2
n
cost of the 1981 algorithm. In 1990, computer scientists proved that no smooth algorithm can do better than log
2
n
. Still, it didn’t seem to make sense to switch to a non-smooth algorithm—after all, if your algorithm intentionally creates spots that are denser than average, your adversary can target those spots and force you to move a lot of books.
“The running belief seemed to become that log
2
n
should be optimal, and that what we should be doing as a community is trying to prove it,” said Kuszmaul.
The focus shifted from looking for new algorithms to proving lower bounds for wider and wider classes of algorithms. In 2012, researchers proved that no deterministic algorithm can improve on log
2
n
. “It’s amazing how strong and robust that bound is,” said Michael Bender, of Stony Brook University, one of the authors of the new paper.
Combined with the earlier results, “This meant that to beat log
2
n
, you had to be both randomized and non-smooth, and you had to do both things in a meaningful way,” Kuszmaul said.

data.title: High-Fidelity Simultaneous Speech-to-Speech Translation
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为Hibiki的解码器模型，用于同声传译，能够同步处理源语言和目标语言的语音，并生成文本和音频标记，实现语音到文本和语音到语音的翻译。该模型通过弱监督方法，利用现成文本翻译系统的困惑度来确定最佳延迟，并创建对齐的合成数据，从而在积累足够上下文后实时翻译。实验表明，Hibiki在法英同声传译任务中，在翻译质量、说话人保真度和自然度方面达到了先进水平，且其推理过程简单，适用于批量翻译和设备上的实时部署。

Abstract:
We introduce Hibiki, a decoder-only model for simultaneous speech translation. Hibiki leverages a multistream language model to synchronously process source and target speech, and jointly produces text and audio tokens to perform speech-to-text and speech-to-speech translation. We furthermore address the fundamental challenge of simultaneous interpretation, which unlike its consecutive counterpart, where one waits for the end of the source utterance to start translating, adapts its flow to accumulate just enough context to produce a correct translation in real-time, chunk by chunk. To do so, we introduce a weakly-supervised method that leverages the perplexity of an off-the-shelf text translation system to identify optimal delays on a per-word basis and create aligned synthetic data. After supervised training, Hibiki performs adaptive, simultaneous speech translation with vanilla temperature sampling. On a French-English simultaneous speech translation task, Hibiki demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in translation quality, speaker fidelity and naturalness. Moreover, the simplicity of its inference process makes it compatible with batched translation and even real-time on-device deployment. We provide examples as well as models and inference code.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕绳索工厂内建造楼梯并将其转变为咖啡馆的艺术项目的讨论，以及对编织工艺、自动化设备及其应用潜力的各种看法。

不同观点：
• [metalman] 认为该项目是一种奇特而有趣的体验，通过复杂的重复动作看到固体物质逐渐成型，并将该设备与“Wind Knitter”归为同一类，即编织设备。
• [lawlessone] 提到购买机器的页面无法工作，且对价格表示担忧，暗示可能无法负担。
• [data-ottawa] 表达了对该项目的喜爱，认为这是令人愉快的怪异项目。
• [MikeTheGreat] 对如何在不散开的情况下“收获”一段管子表示好奇，并提出了具体的操作方法，如切割和有目的的拆解再编织。
• [jkhalaj] 将编织比作编程，认为编织者未得到足够的认可，并将阅读编织图样比作低级编程。
• [stickfigure] 提到该设备与“Hand Tool Rescue”视频中的设备类似，提供了相关视频链接。
• [dmkolobov] 对艺术项目描述中使用的术语表示调侃，认为这是典型的艺术学校用语。
• [socki] 询问该项目是否可以现场观看。
• [jbaber] 提出未来可能的发展方向，如风力纺纱、风力梳理、风力剪毛和风力畜牧，认为有很大的垂直发展机会。
• [boffinAudio] 认为该项目可以用于回收塑料，建议将其应用于海洋塑料回收，并设想在荒岛生存中如何利用这一设备。
• [gcanyon] 对没有Tom Scott的相关视频表示失望。
• [throwaway474843] 希望看到完整的视频过程，并对在线商店的围巾是否完全由风力编织工厂制作表示怀疑，但也表示希望这些围巾确实是通过该项目制作的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于在线商店的围巾是否完全由风力编织工厂制作，[throwaway474843] 对此表示怀疑，认为需要看到完整的视频过程以确认。
• 对该项目应用潜力的讨论，[boffinAudio] 和 [jbaber] 提出了扩大应用范围的建议，如海洋塑料回收和风力操作的其他可能性。
• 对项目技术细节的探讨，[MikeTheGreat] 提出了具体的操作方法，展示了技术上的可行性。

data.title: Manipulating trapped air bubbles in ice for message storage in cold regions
data.author: __rito__
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：冰泡作为数据存储媒介的可行性与相关联想

不同观点：
• **dtgriscom**：认为冰泡作为存储媒介不耐久，不是因为气候变化，而是由于表面能的作用。不同物质之间的边界会随着时间最小化，冰泡最终会变成球体，导致数据无法长期保存。他引用了自己在MIT学到的知识来支持这一观点。
  
• **meindnoch**：提出了一种更有创意的方法，即通过控制树木的年轮来存储信息。每一年可以用覆盖或不覆盖树来分别代表0或1。虽然存储速度很慢（1bit/年），但这一方法引发了对另类存储方式的讨论。

• **0xbadcafebee**：对冰媒介的长期保存性表示怀疑，语气较为调侃。

• **sprior**：将冰泡存储与亚马逊的存储服务类比，戏称为"Amazon Glacier"，带有调侃意味。

• **drfuchs**：通过历史类比，提到1979年的"Intel Magnetics 7110"磁泡存储芯片，暗示冰泡存储可能像过去的技术一样不实用。他还提到了对未来memristor技术的期待。

• **baruchel**：联想到文学作品中"冻结的词语"的概念，提供了文化和文学上的视角。

• **speedylight**：以幽默的方式提到用加热的方式来删除文件，暗示冰泡存储在实际操作中的不便。

• **hnanon12341**：仅仅对文章中的抽象图片表示赞赏，没有深入讨论存储技术本身。

• **lmpdev**：调侃文章本身像是在争取Ig Nobel Prize（搞笑诺贝尔奖），暗示其研究可能不切实际。

• **lloydatkinson**：提到如果要在1925年创建一个冰泡信息并在2025年读取，那么时间旅行是必要的，质疑了实际应用的可能性。

• **Mistletoe**：认为冰泡存储媒介虽然有趣，但实际使用效果可能很差。

• **AlienRobot**：以幽默的方式提到冰泡存储可能在核冬天后会有用，暗示极端环境下的潜在应用。

• **dzink**：对冰泡存储的想法来源表示好奇，但没有深入讨论技术细节。

• **moralestapia**：幽默地表示期待AWS版本的冰泡存储服务，将现代云服务与古老的存储概念结合。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于冰泡作为存储媒介的耐久性和实用性，特别是表面能对冰泡形状的影响。
• 讨论中多次出现幽默和调侃，反映了社区对这一概念实际可行性的普遍怀疑。
• 类比和历史技术（如磁泡存储芯片）的引用丰富了讨论，提供了更多视角。
• 部分评论引入了文化和文学联想，扩展了讨论的范围。

data.title: CO2 sequestration through accelerated weathering of limestone on ships
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：二氧化碳捕集与封存的有效性和可行性

不同观点：
• [vjvjvjvjghv] 认为现有的二氧化碳捕集方法在规模上无法真正对气候变化产生显著影响，因为这些方法需要大量的能源、机械或空间。
• [briandw] 引用了关于使用核爆炸进行大规模碳捕集的研究，并对加速风化的方法表示支持和兴趣，认为这是一个有前景的方向。
• [verisimi] 对通过在船上携带石料来解决二氧化碳问题的方案表示怀疑，认为这不切实际，像是个糟糕的笑话。
• [tocs3] 提出船运的方案虽然能减少二氧化碳排放，但并不能实现负排放，并建议利用旧船通过太阳能和风能进行碳捕集。
• [trhway] 对在船上进行碳捕集的逻辑提出质疑，认为需要考虑石料粉碎、运输等过程中的碳排放，并建议改造旧船以实现半自主运行。
• [moralestapia] 认为许多碳捕集技术在计算“收益”时往往忽略了系统输入所带来的碳排放，例如石料粉碎、运输和燃料补偿等，最终可能导致排放更多碳，并强调无法违背热力学第二定律。
• [comrade1234] 以幽默方式评论，认为如果在船上放几桶酒可能会更好。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于碳捕集技术的实际可行性和规模化能力，尤其是考虑整个过程中隐含的碳排放。
• 讨论中多次提到船运方案的实际操作和潜在问题，包括能源消耗和效率影响。
• [moralestapia] 的评论指出碳捕集技术的理想化模型与现实中碳排放之间的矛盾，强调了系统性考虑的重要性。
• [briandw] 对新技术研究表示乐观，但其他评论者多持怀疑态度。

data.title: Ubuntu 25.10 Raises RISC-V Profile Requirements
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: Canonical计划在Ubuntu 25.10中提升对RISC-V设备的支持，但大多数现有RISC-V设备将无法运行该版本。这是因为Ubuntu 25.10将基准RISC-V配置文件（RVA）从RVA20升级到RVA23，后者要求强制支持向量和虚拟化扩展，以满足更高性能需求如AI、加密和企业工作负载。现有设备如Orange Pi RV2由于缺乏这些扩展将无法支持新版本。不过，Ubuntu 24.04 LTS仍将支持到2029年，因此短期内影响不大。长期来看，这一升级将有助于Ubuntu在RISC-V平台上占据主导地位，但目前支持RVA23的设备还很少。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ubuntu对RISC-V架构的支持及其对硬件的要求

不同观点：
• [shirro] 认为在技术快速发展的背景下，操作系统做出适应未来的决策是合理的，但也有风险。他提到Debian曾将ARM硬浮点系统的最低目标设定为ARMv7，但Raspberry Pi（基于ARMv6）的流行导致问题，最终通过非官方努力解决了问题。这表明在设定最低硬件要求时需要谨慎。

• [somanyphotons] 认为RVA23是一个适合Linux机器的长远ISA选择，而RVA20不是。他提到Ubuntu可能对即将发布的硬件有早期了解，并质疑这种决定是否与RISC-V Android的要求一致。

• [csense] 提出一种技术解决方案，即编写内核补丁或驱动程序来捕获不支持的指令并提供软件实现，从而降低对硬件的严格要求。

• [fithisux] 指出目前还没有面向消费者的RV23主板设备，并提到Orange PI 2存在GFX blob问题，暗示硬件支持的不足可能影响用户体验。

• [Levitating] 表示希望Ubuntu知晓一些未公布的硬件，这表明对Ubuntu当前硬件支持决策的担忧。

• [johnklos] 强烈批评Ubuntu对硬件的高要求，认为这种做法会导致用户流失。他质疑Ubuntu为何在硬件可用之前就做出这些决定，并讽刺地说Ubuntu 25.10可能只能在尚不存在的硬件上运行。

• [throwaway48476] 认为随着RISC-V应用处理器标准的逐步完善，这种问题会不断出现，暗示当前的混乱是技术发展过程中的正常现象。

• [delfinom] 批评Canonical（Ubuntu的开发公司）试图再次分叉一个领域，暗示对Canonical在开源社区中的行为持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Ubuntu决定支持更高规格的RISC-V设备（RVA23）而可能忽略现有设备，这引发了对用户成本和开发者负担的担忧。
• 一些评论者对Ubuntu的决策持批评态度，认为过于激进，而另一些评论者则试图寻找技术解决方案或对未来持观望态度。
• 讨论还涉及Debian的历史经验，为Ubuntu当前的决策提供了对比案例。
• 对RISC-V生态系统中硬件支持和软件兼容性的整体成熟度存在一定的不满和焦虑。

But with a new long-term support (LTS) release looming, it’s rethinking the kind of RISC-V hardware it wants to support going forward.
A recent bug report filed against Ubuntu’s upgrading tool confirmed a major change with regards to the RISC-V requirements for the upcoming Ubuntu 25.10 release — most existing RISC-V devices will
not
be able to run Ubuntu 25.10.
How come?
A New Baseline for RISC-V
Ubuntu 25.10 plans to bumps its baseline RISC-V profile (RVA) from RVA20 to RVA23. It may sound like a small jump but it has a big impact since the bulk of RISC-V devices currently sold don’t support it.
An RVA (RISC-V Application) profile is a specification that outlines the vector processing capabilities a RISC-V system must have, so
“software can rely on the existence of a certain set of […] features in a particular generation of RISC-V implementations”.
That’s according to RISC-V International, the main collaborative group steering and overseeing development of this open source and royalty free processor architecture.
“RISC-V was designed to provide a highly modular and extensible instruction set (ISA) and includes a large and growing set of standard extensions, where each standard extension is a bundle of instruction-set features,”
RISC-V International explains.
The
RVA23 profile
makes a number of ‘extensions’ mandatory, notably
Vector and Hypervisor extensions
to power
“math-intensive workloads including AI/ML & cryptography, and enterprise hardware, operating systems and software workloads
.”
Per Samsung
, the RISC-V ‘V’ Vector extension
“allows CPUs to perform many operations simultaneously, making them faster and more efficient”
. With RVA23 RISC-V reaches a clear feature parity level with ARMv9 and x86-64v4.
It is (naturally) more involved than that. Plenty of
deep-dives on RISC-V Vector extensions
are available online if you find yourself curious about the computational underpinnings and future opportunities they stand to provide.
Impact on Existing Hardware
According to an open issue on Launchpad
, the
“ubuntu-release-upgrader should stop upgrades beyond Ubuntu 24.04 on hardware that does not support the RVA23U64 profile”
, noting that
“RVA23U64 is the profile relevant for user space”
.
Support for earlier versions of Ubuntu on existing RISC-V hadn’t isn’t impacted, but this change does mean that Ubuntu 25.10 (and later) will not run on
most
existing RISC-V hardware (like the
Orange Pi RV2
) since they lack the extensions the RVA23 profile requires.
Will that really be an issue long-term?
Ubuntu 24.04 LTS is supported until 2029 at the earliest and will continue to work on existing hardware, so that’s covered. RISC-V usage remains niche so the impact from Ubuntu ‘raising the bar’ on baseline  profile requirements won’t be huge.
What could be huge is the benefit to Ubuntu going forward.
Focusing future Ubuntu support to devices that have more capable RISC-V profile sets will further position the distro as the
de-facto
OS on the platform. As workload demands increase, and RISC-V hardware becomes more capable and affordable, the opportunities are obvious.
Admittedly there is one big rub: the range of RISC-V devices with RVA23 support is, at the time or writing this, near non-existent. That will change in the coming year, and by the release of Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, the distro will be primed to take full advantage.
RISC-V
Ubuntu 25.10
44431828.article_summary: Canonical计划在Ubuntu 25.10中提升对RISC-V设备的支持，但大多数现有RISC-V设备将无法运行该版本。这是因为Ubuntu 25.10将基准RISC-V配置文件（RVA）从RVA20升级到RVA23，后者要求强制支持向量和虚拟化扩展，以满足更高性能需求如AI、加密和企业工作负载。现有设备如Orange Pi RV2由于缺乏这些扩展将无法支持新版本。不过，Ubuntu 24.04 LTS仍将支持到2029年，因此短期内影响不大。长期来看，这一升级将有助于Ubuntu在RISC-V平台上占据主导地位，但目前支持RVA23的设备还很少。

• 争议的焦点在于Ubuntu决定支持更高规格的RISC-V设备（RVA23）而可能忽略现有设备，这引发了对用户成本和开发者负担的担忧。
• 一些评论者对Ubuntu的决策持批评态度，认为过于激进，而另一些评论者则试图寻找技术解决方案或对未来持观望态度。

主要讨论点：用户对一款名为Jupad的笔记计算工具的功能、使用体验及技术细节的讨论。

不同观点：
• [idanp] 介绍了Jupad工具，并提供了一个概念验证（POC）链接，强调了其使用Python的特点。
• [johncosta27] 对工具的实用性表示赞赏，特别提到其在预算计算方面的便捷性，介于纸笔和完整电子表格之间。
• [zuzzurro] 提出了单位转换和计算中的问题，指出在使用不同时间单位时结果不符合预期，需要转换为秒来计算。
• [xz18r] 推荐了另一款基于mathjs的工具Numerals，强调其在Obsidian中的良好表现和自动求和功能。
• [shepik] 对工具的界面表示赞赏，但指出单位处理中的异常，如"150 kn to km/h"被误认为减法而非转换。
• [zamadatix] 对工具的交互和语法表示赞赏，但对CRDT在同步中的使用提出疑问，担心同步冲突问题。
• [abfar] 指出了计算优先级的问题，例如除法在幂运算前执行，结果与预期不符。
• [kragen] 对工具的UI流程表示赞赏，但关心其代码许可问题，担心版权风险。
• [eviks] 提到工具不支持上标显示，并询问CRDT是否可用于丰富的撤销历史功能，而非仅限于同步。
• [ajjenkins] 对工具的创意和执行表示赞赏，但不确定其实际用途。
• [wslh] 提到寻找其他笔记计算工具时发现了奇怪的产品，提供了一个链接。

补充讨论：
• 用户对工具的单位转换功能有较多讨论，尤其是对结果不符合预期的具体例子进行了详细描述。
• 用户对CRDT技术在工具中的应用表示关注，主要集中在同步冲突和多用户编辑场景下的使用。
• 对计算优先级的疑问反映了用户对数学运算顺序的期望，特别是在不同运算符混合使用时的执行顺序。
• 代码许可和版权问题也被提及，反映了用户在选择工具时对法律风险的关注。

data.title: FossFLOW: Make beautiful isometric infrastructure diagrams
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: FossFLOW是一个开源的渐进式网页应用（PWA），用于创建精美的等距基础设施图。它使用React和Isoflow库构建，完全运行于浏览器中，支持离线使用。主要功能包括自动保存、导入/导出图表、隐私优先（数据存储在本地浏览器中）、以及PWA支持，可在Mac和Linux上作为原生应用安装。用户可以通过拖放组件、连接关系、自定义颜色和标签等方式创建图表，并能管理多个保存的图表。部署时，需注意PWA功能需要HTTPS支持，图表存储在浏览器localStorage中，有5-10MB的限制。项目欢迎贡献，采用Unlicense许可协议。

不同观点：

• [unixhero] 对工具的外观表示赞赏，但更关注其实际功能，特别是是否能够分析AWS基础设施或Proxmox hypervisor环境及其网络。这表明他希望该工具具备较强的技术分析能力，而不仅仅是展示功能。

• [dddw] 对工具表示了简单的认可，并表示愿意尝试，没有提出具体的技术需求或功能要求，态度较为中立和积极。

补充讨论：
• [anonzzzies] 提出的工具需求是一个潜在的扩展功能，即从Mermaid markup代码到演示文稿的转换工具，目前似乎难以找到现成的解决方案。

• [unixhero] 的评论指向了实际应用中的技术需求，特别是对云基础设施（AWS）和虚拟化环境（Proxmox）的分析功能，这可能涉及到工具的功能扩展或与其他工具的集成。

• 当前讨论中并没有直接的争议，但存在不同的关注点。[anonzzzies] 关心工具的格式转换功能，[unixhero] 则更关心工具在实际技术环境中的应用能力，而[dddw] 则表现出对工具的一般性兴趣和尝试意愿。

FossFLOW - Isometric Diagramming Tool
FossFLOW is a powerful, open-source Progressive Web App (PWA) for creating beautiful isometric diagrams. Built with React and the Isoflow (Now forked and published to NPM as fossflow) library, it runs entirely in your browser with offline support.
📝
FOSSFLOW_TODO.md
- Current issues and roadmap with codebase mappings, most gripes are with the isoflow library itself.
🤝
CONTRIBUTORS.md

Features
🎨
Isometric Diagramming
- Create stunning 3D-style technical diagrams
💾
Auto-Save
- Your work is automatically saved every 5 seconds
📱
PWA Support
- Install as a native app on Mac and Linux
🔒
Privacy-First
- All data stored locally in your browser
📤
Import/Export
- Share diagrams as JSON files
🎯
Session Storage
- Quick save without dialogs
🌐
Offline Support
- Work without internet connection
Quick Start
#
Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/stan-smith/FossFLOW
cd
FossFLOW
#
Make sure you have npm installed
#
Install dependencies
npm install
#
Start development server
npm start
Open
http://localhost:3000
in your browser.
How to Use
Creating Diagrams
Add Items
: Drag and drop components from the library onto the canvas
Connect Items
: Use connectors to show relationships between components
Customize
: Change colors, labels, and properties of items
Navigate
: Pan and zoom to work on different areas
Saving Your Work
Auto-Save
: Diagrams are automatically saved to browser storage every 5 seconds
Quick Save
: Click "Quick Save (Session)" for instant saves without popups
Save As

Managing Diagrams
Load

Import
: Load diagrams from JSON files shared by others
Export
: Download your diagrams as JSON files to share or backup
Storage
: Use "Storage Manager" to manage browser storage space

Delete
- Remove selected items
Mouse wheel - Zoom in/out
Click and drag - Pan around canvas

44458378.article_summary: FossFLOW是一个开源的渐进式网页应用（PWA），用于创建精美的等距基础设施图。它使用React和Isoflow库构建，完全运行于浏览器中，支持离线使用。主要功能包括自动保存、导入/导出图表、隐私优先（数据存储在本地浏览器中）、以及PWA支持，可在Mac和Linux上作为原生应用安装。用户可以通过拖放组件、连接关系、自定义颜色和标签等方式创建图表，并能管理多个保存的图表。部署时，需注意PWA功能需要HTTPS支持，图表存储在浏览器localStorage中，有5-10MB的限制。项目欢迎贡献，采用Unlicense许可协议。

data.title: Experiment: Colocating agent instructions with eng docs
data.author: dannyrosen
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了将AI代理指令嵌入工程师文档中的实验。作者最初对单独维护代理文档持怀疑态度，因为这可能导致信息重复和不同步。为此，作者尝试将代理指令嵌入现有的工程师文档（如`examples.rst`）的注释中，而非创建单独的文档（如`GEMINI.md`）。实验中，作者使用Gemini CLI根据文档中的指令迁移代码示例，结果显示代理严格遵循了嵌入的指令，甚至捕捉到了文档中的一个错误。尽管实验成功，但作者指出，若仓库中完全没有单独的代理文档，结果可能会有所不同。实验表明，将代理指令嵌入现有工程师文档可能是一种有效的解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在工程项目中有效记录和利用LLM（大型语言模型）和AI助手的使用日志及指令

不同观点：
• **jauntywundrkind** 认为，默认将aider日志添加到`.gitignore`并不理想。他主张保留这些日志，以便人类和AI都能从中反思和学习。他建议将AI指令与工程文档一起保存，并提出可以利用像Backstage这样的工具来集成和管理这些知识库。他还提到了MCP服务器用于反思聊天历史的可能性，并对Kenton Varda和Cloudflare在该领域的实践表示赞赏。

• **8note** 对jauntywundrkind的观点表示支持和兴奋，特别强调了让LLM在不同工程师之间保持可重复性的重要性。他赞同保留日志和指令的想法，认为这有助于提高团队协作和知识共享的效率。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：是否应该默认忽略aider日志。jauntywundrkind认为忽略日志对人类和AI都不利，而默认设置是忽略这些日志。
• **技术工具的建议**：jauntywundrkind提到了Backstage和MCP服务器的潜在应用，特别是如何通过这些工具来更好地组织和管理AI助手和LLM的使用记录。
• **实际案例**：Kenton Varda和Cloudflare的项目被当作一个好的实践例子，用于展示如何记录和推广AI指令作为参考材料。

通过这些讨论，可以看出社区对于如何在工程中有效利用和记录LLM及AI助手的使用持有不同但积极的看法，并提出了具体的工具和方法建议。

44423194.article_content:
(Experiment) Colocating agent instructions with eng docs
§
In my initial investigation of agent docs (
Docs for AI agents
) I expressed
skepticism over the current design of agent docs.  Agent providers like Claude
Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and so on are steering us towards maintaining agent
docs as a new docs set, separate from preexisting internal eng docs. I worry
that we’ll end up duplicating a lot of information across the two docs sets.
Inevitably, the duplicated information gets out-of-sync with each other.
In
Colocate
, I basically propose embedding the agent instructions
within the internal eng docs.  I tried out the colocate solution today, and the
results were promising. Here are the details.
Background
§
Today on
pigweed.dev
, we published
Guidelines for buildable and testable code examples
.
At the top of the page, I embedded AI agent instructions:
.. Instructions for AI agents (e.g. Gemini CLI):
.. #. Follow the workflow described in :ref:`contributing-docs-quickstart-a`.
..    Do not use Option B.
.. #. Inspect the files in ``//pw_string/examples``. This is a working example
..    of the kind of code that you need to create.
.. #. Create the code example, unit test, and build targets. The first
..    iteration of the unit test should fail.
.. #. Run ``bazelisk test //...`` to verify that your new unit test fails.
.. #. Fix the unit test.
.. #. Run ``bazelisk test //...`` again and verify that the new unit test now
..    passes.
.. _contributing-docs-examples:
===================================================
Guidelines for buildable and testable code examples
===================================================
This guide shows :ref:`docs-glossary-upstream` maintainers how to write
buildable and testable code examples for ``pigweed.dev``. It's focused on
C++ but the general pattern is theoretically applicable to any language.
…
(See
examples.rst
to view the full source code.)
All of those lines at the top of the file beginning with
..
are
comments. Humans viewing the page on a web browser don’t see those comments.
These comments are the instructions for the agent. I embedded them within
the eng doc, rather than spinning up a separate agent doc like
CLAUDE.md
,
GEMINI.md
,
AGENTS.md
, etc.
Experiment
§
I loaded up the code examples guidelines (
@docs/contributing/docs/examples.rst
)
and then instructed Gemini CLI to migrate a specific code example:
> @docs/contributing/docs/examples.rst use the instructions in examples.rst to
convert the code example in the "Known size string" section of pw_string/guide.rst
into a buildable and testable code example. Note that the examples.rst instructions
has a mistake. When you update the sphinx_docs_library Bazel rules, you should
update the `srcs` list, not the `deps` list.
Results
§
It worked really well. Gemini CLI closely followed the agent instructions
that I provided. Specifically:
I told Gemini CLI to first create a failing test, verify that the test fails,
and then fix it. It did exactly that.
I got inadvertent confirmation that Gemini CLI was following my instructions
closely. There’s a mistake in
examples.rst
. It instructs you to update
the
deps
list in the
sphinx_docs_library
. You actually need to update
the
srcs
list. The first time I tried this workflow, Gemini CLI got
confused because it could not find a
deps
list on the rule.
Caveats:
This was an informal experiment. To properly control the experiment, the
repo should have no agent docs, i.e. no
GEMINI.md
files. This was not
the case. The Pigweed repo has an extensive agent doc, as you can see in
the logs after I run the
/memory
show
command. So, it’s still not clear
whether the agent would successfully complete the task if given only colocated
instructions. In other words, maybe this experiment is suggesting that you
get the best results when you have both agent docs and more targeted
instructions.
Below is the full log. See
pwrev.dev/301461/1
to view the code that Gemini CLI
generated.

data.article_summary: 这个夏天，由奥斯卡获奖导演昆汀·塔伦蒂诺拥有的维斯塔剧院将放映《杀死比尔》的加长版《Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair》。这部时长258分钟的导演剪辑版将于7月18日至28日在大银幕上以35毫米格式放映。该版本曾在2006年戛纳电影节上亮相，包含法语字幕和中场休息，是塔伦蒂诺最初为观众设想的完整版。与原版电影相比，这个版本包含一些不同的镜头，如仅在日本版中出现的画面、编辑过的悬念和附加的动画片段。门票现已开始预售，票价为21美元。放映地点为维斯塔剧院，时间为7月18日至28日，每天有12:30和19:30两场放映。

,

data.author: Arubis

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲与美国之间技术工作者移民、薪资和生活质量的比较

不同观点：
• [0xfaded] 认为如果在欧洲找到一份薪资高于平均水平的工作，移民到理想的欧洲国家并不难，尤其是对技术工作者来说。他建议先在美国赚钱，然后为了更好的生活质量或价值观迁移到欧洲。他还提到迁移财富时可能遇到的税务问题（如退出税）。
   
• [drdunce] 持相反观点，认为欧盟的科技人才市场已经饱和，对高需求技术专业人士的需求不大。

• [j7ake] 质疑为什么只关注科技行业，建议寻找欧盟薪资比美国更好的其他行业。

• [ldjkfkdsjnv] 回应[j7ake]的评论，提到外包公司如Wipro、Infosys、Cognizant是可能的选项，但暗示这些工作的薪资低且内容乏味。

• [android521] 同意[ldjkfkdsjnv]的观点，进一步指出这些工作不仅薪资低，而且工作内容无趣。

• [throwawaysleep] 认为对于研究型人才，欧盟有更大的机会，并指出直到今年人们还主要从欧盟流向美国。

• [keiferski] 提到Nomad Capitalist这个人正在实践这种迁移策略。

• [scarface_74] 质疑为什么要去薪资低、税高、生活成本却不低的国家，认为没有足够的理由离开美国。

• [dmitrygr] 支持[scarface_74]的观点，认为找到薪资和美国一样高、且生活质量更好的地方不容易，并指出离开美国的决定说起来容易，做起来难。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到迁移财富时的税务问题，特别是“退出税”，这是迁移过程中的一个实际障碍。
• 不同评论者对欧盟科技人才市场的供需情况有不同看法，有的认为市场饱和，有的则认为对特定人才仍有需求。
• 对工作内容和薪资的讨论，尤其是外包公司的工作，显示出对某些职位的负面看法。
• 总体而言，评论反映了对生活质量、价值观和薪资之间权衡的复杂考虑。

data.title: How AI on Microcontrollers Works: Operators and Kernels
data.author: hasheddan
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了在微控制器上运行边缘AI（edge AI）推理的实际能力以及新硬件进展的影响。边缘AI通常涉及在计算、内存或网络带宽受限的硬件上执行推理。文章重点介绍了TensorFlow Lite for Microcontrollers（现已更名为LiteRT for Microcontrollers），这是一个用于微控制器的优化推理 runtime。它使用 `.tflite` 文件格式，通过 FlatBuffers 编码数据，包含模型权重和计算图。

文章还解释了运算符（operators）和内核（kernels）的概念，运算符定义了推理操作，而内核则是这些运算符的软件实现，具体性能取决于硬件支持。例如，加法运算符（TFL::AddOp）的实现会根据输出类型（如 `kTfLiteInt8` 或 `kTfLiteInt16`）选择不同的计算方法。文章通过代码示例展示了 `AddEval()` 函数如何处理不同数据类型的加法操作，强调了硬件对性能的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否需要为微控制器设计专门的"lite"格式，或者是否可以统一使用像ONNX这样的通用格式

不同观点：
• [amelius] 认为不需要为微控制器专门设计"lite"格式，并提出统一使用ONNX格式的建议。其主要论据是，ONNX作为一个通用的深度学习模型格式，可能足以应对各种需求，包括微控制器上的应用。他还提供了ONNX的官方链接供参考。

• [Neywiny] 则持不同意见，认为"嵌入式"和"边缘"计算的概念是相对的，具体应用场景差异很大。他指出，对于不同的场景，"边缘AI"可能意味着从服务器场到传感器等不同层次的设备。因此，针对微控制器设计专门的解决方案是有必要的，因为不同设备的计算能力和资源各不相同，不能一概而论。

补充讨论：
• [Neywiny] 进一步解释了"边缘AI"在不同场景下的多样性，比如在一些情况下，边缘AI可能指的是本地服务器场，而在另一些情况下，可能指的是传感器中的微控制器。这种多样性意味着，不可能用一个单一的解决方案（如ONNX）来满足所有需求。

• 争议的焦点在于是否需要为微控制器设计专门的格式。一方认为统一格式（如ONNX）可以简化开发和部署，另一方则认为不同设备需要不同的解决方案，以适应其硬件限制和应用场景。

• 论据中提到了设备资源和计算能力的差异，这是支持专门"lite"格式的主要理由，而统一格式的支持者则强调标准化和兼容性的优势。

44422662.article_content:
The buzz around “edge AI”, which means something slightly different to almost
everyone you talk to, is well past reaching a fever pitch. Regardless of what
edge AI means to you, the one commonality is typically that the hardware on
which inference is being performed is constrained in one or more dimensions,
whether it be compute, memory, or network bandwidth. Perhaps the most
constrained of these platforms are microcontrollers.
I have found that, while there is much discourse around “running AI” (i.e.
performing inference) on microcontrollers, there is a general lack of
information about what these systems are actually capable of, and how new
hardware advancements impact that equation. It is my hope with this series to
peel back some of the layers of terminology and explore what actually happens
between supplying inputs to a model and receiving outputs. Along the way, we’ll
ground our exploration in performing inference with real models on real
constrained hardware.
While “weights” get the majority of the attention with AI models, they alone are
not sufficient for performing inference. Depending on how a model is distributed
and what runtime is used, additional data or metadata may be supplied alongside
the model, or may be defined explicitly in software that interacts with the
weights. The most popular runtime for microcontrollers is
Tensorflow Lite for
Microcontrollers
(
tflite-micro
)
,
which is an optimized version of
Tensorflow
Lite
.
Note: Google recently
rebranded Tensorflow Lite to
LiteRT
,
and
tflite-micro
to LiteRT for Microcontrollers.
tflite-micro
uses the
.tflite
file format, which encodes data using
FlatBuffers
. Unlike some other model file formats,
.tflite
files include not only the tensors that encapuslate model weights, but
also the
computation graph
, which informs the runtime of what operations to
use when performing inference. In order to do so, there needs to be a defined
set of
operators
. This is somewhat analagous to instructions defined in an
instruction set architecture
(ISA)
for a
processor. With an ISA, a compiler will take a higher level programming language
and map the behavior onto instructions available in the ISA. Tensorflow supports
an extensive set of
built-in
operators
, while Tensorflow Lite, and
thus
tflite-micro
, supports
only a
subset
.
Continuing the analaogy, many processors implement specific versions of the
ARM
architecture
, but that
doesn’t mean that processors implementing the same ISA are equivalent. Every
instruction that is supported has to be implemented in hardware, and decisions
about how the processor is designed can impact performance on multiple
dimensions. Similarly, while Tensorflow Lite defines a set of operators, the
implementation of those operators, which are referred to as
kernels
, may vary.
Kernels are implemented in software, but depending on the underlying hardware, a
kernel might take many instructions to execute, or may be able to optimized to
leverage dedicated hardware support.
A simple example is the
addition operator
(
TFL::AddOp
)
. We’ll
cover how operators and kernels are registered and invoked in a future post, but
let’s start by taking a look at the default
tflite-micro
addition operator
logic.
tensorflow/lite/micro/kernels/add.cc

(output->type == kTfLiteFloat32 || output->type == kTfLiteInt32) {
TF_LITE_ENSURE_OK(
context, EvalAdd(context, node, params, data, input1, input2, output));
}
else
if
(output->type == kTfLiteInt8 || output->type == kTfLiteInt16) {

input1, input2, output));
}
else
{
MicroPrintf(
"Type %s (%d) not supported."
, TfLiteTypeGetName(output->type),
output->type);

kTfLiteError;
}

kTfLiteOk;
}
TFLMRegistration Register_ADD() {
return
tflite::micro::RegisterOp(AddInit, AddPrepare, AddEval);
}
As can be observed in
AddEval()
, the type of output we are expecting
influences the implementation of the operator. To illustrate how the underlying
hardware impacts performance, let’s focus on the case in which we expect
kTfLiteInt8
(signed 8-bit integer) or
kTfLiteInt16
(signed 16-bit integer)
output, meaning that we’ll call
EvalAddQuantized()
.
