data.title: WASM Agents: AI agents running in the browser
data.author: selvan
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个名为 **Wasm agents blueprint** 的实验性项目，旨在通过将代理编写为 HTML 文件，使其能够在浏览器中直接运行，而无需额外安装工具或框架。该项目利用 **WebAssembly** 和 **Pyodide** 技术，将 Python 代码在浏览器中运行，实现了一种轻量、跨平台的 AI 代理。项目中的每个代理都是独立的 HTML 文件，包含用户界面和运行代码，使用 **openai-agents-python** 库与 LLM（如 GPT-4）进行交互，也可以接入自托管模型（如通过 Ollama 或 HuggingFace 提供的模型）。项目提供了多个示例，包括简单对话代理、多代理系统和带有工具的代理等，展示了 Wasm 代理的潜力。用户可以通过 GitHub 获取代码并按照说明运行这些代理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在浏览器中运行AI代理和相关技术的可行性及其实现方法

不同观点：
• simonw：认为文中的"agent"定义来源于OpenAI的Python库，该库将工具作为可选项，而不是必选项，这与许多其他代理定义不同。他还指出"hello world"演示仅运行单个提示。
• thepoet：提到他们在评估Pyodide和WASM时发现多步骤任务需要本地运行LLM生成的代码，并选择了Apple Containers上的CodeRunner，但认为在处理任意提示方面仍需改进。
• meander_water：认为直接在浏览器中运行模型更有趣，可以通过transformers.js和onnx runtime实现，且无需GPU。
• om8：展示了在浏览器中运行llama3模型的demo，并建议未来可以完全本地化。
• TekMol：质疑为何需要WASM，因为当前仅运行与服务器LLM通信的代码。
• ipsum2：分享了通过修改JS绕过网站反自动化点击检测的经验，并认为Firefox由于其可扩展性可能成为代理的未来。
• _pdp_：认为用Python编写客户端代码并没有简化代理创建，反而更复杂。他还指出代理连接工具并嵌入工作流仅是工作的一小部分，更多的工作在于可观察性、后台任务、队列系统等。
• asim：认为代理应是长期运行的外部浏览器进程，WASM的想法聪明但浏览器环境需要进化。
• sandGorgon：介绍了他们在移动浏览器中创建AI代理的经验，并提到通过扩展框架实现这些代理，且在Android上实现更困难。
• benatkin：认为文章试图用"agent"这个词来显得酷，但并未说明为何这不仅仅是基础AI工作，指出openai-agents-python库可用于编写非代理代码。
• raybb：询问是否可以通过浏览器扩展绕过CORS问题。
• zoobab：指出未提及WebGPU。
• dncornholio：认为在HTML文件中将Python代码放入字符串是过时的做法。
• _joel：理解为何需要禁用CORS限制，但仍觉得这不太理想。

补充讨论：
• 关于是否需要WASM的争议（simonw, TekMol）。
• 在浏览器中直接运行模型的可行性和工具选择（meander_water, om8, meander_water）。
• 对代理定义及其实际应用的讨论（simonw, _pdp_, benatkin）。
• 绕过技术限制（如CORS）的实际操作经验（ipsum2, raybb）。
• 对不同技术栈（如Python、WebGPU）在浏览器中应用的看法（zoobab, dncornholio）。

44461341.article_content:
One of the main barriers to a wider adoption and experimentation with open-source agents is the dependency on extra tools and frameworks that need to be installed before the agents can be run. In this post, we introduce the
Wasm agents blueprint
, aimed at showing how to write agents as HTML files, which can just be opened and run in a browser, without the need for any extra dependencies. This is still an experimental project, but we chose to share it early so that people can both test its capabilities and build new applications based on it.
Why?
While developing our
agent-factory
tool, we have been wondering about ways to package an agent so it could be easily shared and executed on different systems. In the past, we addressed a similar problem with
marimo
, both when trying to
convey our thoughts with code examples
and when introducing
new tools for algorithmic timelines
. In both cases, the main advantage was that people could run code directly on their devices, more precisely inside their own browsers, thanks to the possibility of exporting marimo notebooks as standalone HTML files powered by
WebAssembly
and
Pyodide
.
WebAssembly
(Wasm) is a binary instruction format that allows code written in languages like C, C++, Rust, and Python to run at near-native speed in web browsers.
Pyodide
is a Python distribution for the browser that runs entirely in WebAssembly, enabling you to execute Python code and many of its libraries directly in web applications. As most of our agentic code is in Python, it was quite natural for us to think about adopting a similar solution: the result is a collection of simple, single-file agents that run in a browser tab, in an environment that is sandboxed by construction, and without the need to manually install extra libraries or development frameworks.
How it works
All our demos are standalone HTML files, which contain both the UI and the running code of an agent. If you look at their source code, you will see three calls to the
pyodide.runPythonAsync
command. They deal, respectively, with installing the required Python dependencies (with the
micropip
customisation Pyodide library); disabling traces (this is currently required only when running the openai-agents framework – you can find more information in the customization section below); and running the actual agent code.
The agent code is nothing more than a Python script that relies on the
openai-agents-python
library to run an AI agent backed by an LLM served via an OpenAI-compatible API. What this means is that while it runs with OpenAI out-of-the-box (using gpt-4o as a default model), you can also specify a different, self-hosted model, as long as it is compatible with the API. This includes, for instance, models served via
HuggingFace TGI
,
vLLM
, or even
Ollama
running locally on your computer.
Give it a try
If you want to try our agents, follow the
setup instructions
in our GitHub repo. The TL/DR is: if you have a ready-to-use OpenAI API key, you can just paste it into the provided config.js file. If instead you want to try a local model, you should make sure that it is running and that you know the URL to access it. For example, if you want to run qwen3:8b on Ollama, you should first download the application, then the model (with Ollama pull qwen3:8b). After that, open one of the HTML files in your browser and follow the instructions provided: your agent should be up and running in a few seconds.
What can I do?
Our demos show some of the things you can do with Wasm agents, but I think we just scratched the surface of what one could do! So take these as just some examples you can start with, and play with them to test their capabilities, and learn how to build new applications with them. In the
/demos
directory, you will find the following HTML files:
hello_agent.html
: This is a simple conversational agent with customizable instructions, useful for understanding the basics of WASM-based agents.
handoff_demo.html
: a multi-agent system that routes requests to specialized agents based on the characteristics of the prompt.
tool_calling.html
: A more advanced agent with built-in tools for (more or less) practical tasks. The
count_character_occurrences
tool addresses the famous "How many Rs in strawberry?" problem. The
visit_webpage
tool downloads web content and converts it to markdown, and can be used by the agent to seek up-to-date information about the question directly on the web.
ollama_local.html
: An agent which relies on local models served via Ollama, good for offline tasks or when you don’t want your information to leak to external AI services.
NOTE: If you want to run tools that get information from some other server into your HTML page (e.g. the
visit_webpage
tool or the Ollama server itself), you need to make sure that CORS is enabled for those servers. For more information, refer to the
troubleshooting
section in our GitHub repository.

data.title: Zig breaking change – initial Writergate
data.author: Retro_Dev
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Zig编程语言中的一个重大变更，主要涉及标准输入输出（std.io）的读者（Reader）和写者（Writer）接口。新的`std.io.Reader`和`std.io.Writer`不再使用泛型，但在接口内包含缓冲区，以优化性能。变更非常重大，尤其影响格式化打印功能。多个旧的API被弃用或删除，如`std.fs.File.reader`改为`std.fs.File.deprecatedReader`等。文章提供了升级指南，帮助开发者将旧API适配到新API，并介绍了新的便捷功能和独特概念，如读取时的丢弃（discarding）和写入时的散布（splatting），以及文件句柄的关键信息缓存等。这些变更旨在提高性能和易用性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zig语言的 breaking changes 及其影响

不同观点：
• **dnautics** 认为 Zig 的 breaking changes 并没有造成太大困扰。作为 Zig 与 Elixir 接口库的维护者，他通过自动化测试和代码扫描来快速应对变化，且感觉近年来 breaking changes 影响变小、变少。他认为抱怨 changes 的人并非 Zig 的日常用户。同时，他指出新手可能因为网上过时的示例代码而遇到困难。
  
• **mtlynch** 表达了对 breaking changes 的失望，尤其是在 Zig 0.12.0 版本中构建系统的重大变化未得到充分解释，导致下游开发者无所适从。他希望 Zig 团队在未来能提供更好的迁移指导。

• **ww520** 关注旧的 reader/writer 模式在结构体中存储的困难，并询问新变化是否解决了这一问题。

• **dnautics** 再次对新的 API 设计提出疑问，特别是关于异步函数中的 suspend 点是否仍然支持，并询问用户是否能构建带有 yield 点的函数。

• **90s_dev** 表示可以接受 breaking changes，只要能在一天内解决。相比 C/C++ 的跨平台编译困难，Zig 如果能解决这一问题将非常有吸引力。

• **Aissen** 建议 Zig 应该有自动化工具来处理语言和标准库的语义变化，类似于 Go 的 `go fix` 工具，以帮助开发者应对 breaking changes。

• **blippage** 分享了尝试 Zig 用于微控制器项目时的负面体验，由于语法变化和依赖更新，最终选择回归 C，并认为 C 在低级编程中难以被超越。

• **brabel** 认为 Zig 不断重新设计自己，而其他语言如 Odin 早已“出货”，质疑 Zig 是否陷入了完美主义综合症。

补充讨论：
• **thrwyexecbrain** 对新的 `Reader.stream` 和 `Writer.sendFile` API 表示赞赏，认为其设计优雅，适用于构建基于推送的数据转换管道。

• **kristoff_it** 提供了 Zig 2026 路线图的视频链接，为讨论提供了背景信息。

• **ksynwa** 和 **GolDDranks** 的评论较为轻松，前者开玩笑询问 "Writergate" 是否为技术术语，后者表示虽然目前对 Zig 的 breaking changes 持谨慎态度，但仍期待其稳定版本，同时继续使用 Rust。

争议焦点：
• Breaking changes 的合理性及其对开发者的影响是主要争议点。一部分开发者（如 dnautics）认为影响不大，而另一部分开发者（如 mtlynch）则认为缺乏足够的迁移指导，给开发者带来了困扰。

• Zig 是否过度追求完美，导致频繁 redesign 而未能稳定发布，也是讨论中的一个争议点。

Previous Scandal
Summary
Deprecates all existing std.io readers and writers in favor of the newly provided
std.io.Reader
and
std.io.Writer
which are
non-generic
and have the buffer above the vtable - in other words the buffer is
in the interface, not the implementation
. This means that although Reader and Writer are no longer generic, they are still transparent to optimization; all of the interface functions have a concrete hot path operating on the buffer, and only make vtable calls when the buffer is full.
I have a lot more changes to upstream but it was taking too long to finish them so I decided to do it more piecemeal. Therefore, I opened this tiny baby PR to get things started.
These changes are extremely breaking. I am sorry for that, but I have carefully examined the situation and acquired confidence that this is the direction that Zig needs to go. I hope you will strap in your seatbelt and come along for the ride; it will be worth it.
The breakage in this first PR mainly has to do with formatted printing.
Upgrade Guide
Turn on
-freference-trace
to help you find all the format string breakage.
std.fs.File.reader -> std.fs.File.deprecatedReader
std.fs.File.writer -> std.fs.File.deprecatedWriter
std.fmt.format -> std.fmt.deprecatedFormat
std.fmt.fmtSliceEscapeLower -> std.ascii.hexEscape
std.fmt.fmtSliceEscapeUpper -> std.ascii.hexEscape
std.fmt.fmtSliceHexLower -> {x}
std.fmt.fmtSliceHexUpper -> {X}
std.fmt.fmtIntSizeDec -> {B}
std.fmt.fmtIntSizeBin -> {Bi}
std.fmt.fmtDuration -> {D}
std.fmt.fmtDurationSigned -> {D}
{} -> {f} when there is a format method. This prevents footguns when adding or deleting format methods.
format method signature
anytype -> *std.io.Writer
inferred error set -> error{WriteFailed}
FormatOptions -> (deleted)
std.fmt.Formatter
now takes context type explicitly
no fmt string
These are deprecated but not deleted yet:
std.io.GenericReader -> std.io.Reader
std.io.GenericWriter -> std.io.Writer
std.io.AnyReader -> std.io.Reader
std.io.AnyWriter -> std.io.Writer
If you have an old stream and you need a new one, you can use

like this:

foo

old_writer

try
w
.

}
New API
Formatted Printing
{t} is shorthand for
@tagName()
and
@errorName()
{b64}: output string as standard base64
std.io.Writer
and
std.io.Reader
These have a bunch of handy new APIs that are more convenient, perform better, and are not generic. For instance look at how reading until a delimiter works now.
These streams also feature some unique concepts compared with other languages' stream implementations:
The concept of
discarding
when reading: allows efficiently ignoring data. For instance a decompression stream, when asked to discard a large amount of data, can skip decompression of entire frames.
The concept of
splatting
when writing: this allows a logical "memset" operation to pass through I/O pipelines without actually doing any memory copying, turning an O(M*N) operation into O(M) operation, where M is the number of streams in the pipeline and N is the number of repeated bytes. In some cases it can be even more efficient, such as when splatting a zero value that ends up being written to a file; this can be lowered as a seek forward.
Sending a file when writing: this allows an I/O pipeline to do direct fd-to-fd copying when the operating system supports it.
The stream user provides the buffer, but the stream implementation decides the minimum buffer size. This effectively moves state from the stream implementation into the user's buffer
std.fs.File.Reader
Memoizes key information about a file handle such as:
The size from calling stat, or the error that occurred therein.
The current seek position.
The error that occurred when trying to seek.
Whether reading should be done positionally or streaming.
Whether reading should be done via fd-to-fd syscalls (e.g.
sendfile
)
versus plain variants (e.g.
read
).

std.io.Reader

• **thrwyexecbrain** 对新的 `Reader.stream` 和 `Writer.sendFile` API 表示赞赏，认为其设计优雅，适用于构建基于推送的数据转换管道。

• **kristoff_it** 提供了 Zig 2026 路线图的视频链接，为讨论提供了背景信息。

• **ksynwa** 和 **GolDDranks** 的评论较为轻松，前者开玩笑询问 "Writergate" 是否为技术术语，后者表示虽然目前对 Zig 的 breaking changes 持谨慎态度，但仍期待其稳定版本，同时继续使用 Rust。

争议焦点：
• Breaking changes 的合理性及其对开发者的影响是主要争议点。一部分开发者（如 dnautics）认为影响不大，而另一部分开发者（如 mtlynch）则认为缺乏足够的迁移指导，给开发者带来了困扰。

• Zig 是否过度追求完美，导致频繁 redesign 而未能稳定发布，也是讨论中的一个争议点。

44461222.article_content:
News | 01 July 2025
Major reversal in ocean circulation detected in the Southern Ocean, with key climate implications
Share
Newsletter
Satellite data processing algorithms developed by ICM-CSIC have played a crucial role in detecting this significant shift in the Southern Hemisphere, which could accelerate the effects of climate change.
The reversal of ocean circulation in the southern hemisphere could double current atmospheric concentrations of CO₂ / ICM-CSIC.
Thanks to data obtained from Earth observation satellites, an international team of scientists has detected an unprecedented phenomenon for the first time: a reversal in the ocean circulation of the Southern Ocean. The study, led by the National Oceanographic Center (NOC, United Kingdom), was recently published in the journal
PNAS
. The Institut de Ciències del Mar (ICM-CSIC) played a fundamental role in the research by developing a set of pioneering satellite observations within the framework of the SO-FRESH project, funded by the European Space Agency (ESA).
The study’s main finding is both surprising and alarming: since 2016, a sustained increase in surface salinity has been detected in the region between the polar and subpolar gyres of the Antarctic Ocean. This change in water composition suggests that the deep ocean circulation in the Southern Hemisphere—known as the SMOC—is not only being altered, but has reversed. That is, instead of sinking into the depths, surface water is being replaced by deep water masses rising to the surface, bringing with them heat and carbon dioxide (CO₂) that had been trapped for centuries.
“We are witnessing a true reversal of ocean circulation in the Southern Hemisphere—something we’ve never seen before,” explains
Antonio Turiel
, ICM-CSIC researcher and co-author of the study. “While the world is debating the potential collapse of the AMOC in the North Atlantic, we’re seeing that the SMOC is not just weakening, but has reversed. This could have unprecedented global climate impacts.”
According to the research team, the consequences of this reversal are already becoming visible. The upwelling of deep, warm, CO₂-rich waters is believed to be driving the accelerated melting of sea ice in the Southern Ocean. In the long term, this process could double current atmospheric CO₂ concentrations by releasing carbon that has been stored in the deep ocean for centuries—potentially with catastrophic consequences for the global climate.
This discovery was made possible thanks to a key technical breakthrough developed by the Barcelona Expert Center (BEC), a laboratory of ICM-CSIC specialized in satellite ocean observation. Until now, the Southern Ocean region was virtually inaccessible to satellites due to its low temperatures and the complex, ever-changing dynamics of sea ice. As a result, the BEC team developed a new data processor for the European SMOS satellite, tailored to the geographical and climatic variability of the polar environment.
“The new processor has allowed us to obtain surface salinity data of unprecedented quality in this region,” explains
Verónica González
. “Thanks to this improvement, we can now provide a coherent explanation for the rapid Antarctic sea ice loss that had puzzled the scientific community.”
The study not only provides a key piece in the climate change puzzle, but also redefines the role of the Southern Ocean in the global climate system. The SMOC plays an essential role in regulating the planet’s heat and carbon. Its disruption could trigger cascading effects on other circulation systems such as the AMOC, with potential consequences for the climate in Europe and other regions.
Aware of the urgent need to better understand these processes, BEC has launched two new ESA-funded projects in 2025: ARCTIC-FLOW, focused on the study of freshwater and density fluxes in the Arctic Ocean, and the climate change initiative CCI OSHF (Ocean Surface Heat Flux), dedicated to analyzing heat fluxat the ocean surface. Both projects aim to develop new satellite methodologies that will be key to monitoring, understanding, and anticipating the effects of accelerated climate change.
“The planet is sending us increasingly clear signals that we are crossing critical thresholds,” concludes
Estrella Olmedo
. “And in this case, it has done so from a remote corner of the world that is very difficult to monitor: the Southern Ocean. Thanks to satellites and cutting-edge observation tools, we can now see what was once invisible.”
Reference article
Alessandro Silvano; Aditya Narayanan; Rafael Catany, et al. (2025).
Rising surface salinity and declining sea ice: A new Southern Ocean state revealed by satellites
. PNAS. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2500440122

data.title: Context Engineering for Agents
data.author: 0x79de
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在构建大型语言模型（LLM）应用时，情境工程（Context Engineering）的重要性。情境窗口如同CPU的RAM，容量有限，需要精心管理以确保代理（agent）有效执行任务。情境工程涉及管理多种类型的情境信息，包括指令、知识和工具反馈。

文章将情境工程策略分为四类：
1. **写入情境**：将情境信息保存在情境窗口之外，例如使用“草稿纸”（Scratchpad）来存储中间结果。
2. **选择情境**：从草稿纸或运行时状态中选择相关信息加入情境窗口。
3. **压缩情境**：通过摘要或精简方式减少情境信息量。
4. **隔离情境**：避免不相关或冲突的信息进入情境窗口。

这些策略帮助解决长时任务中的情境中毒、分心、混淆和冲突等问题，是开发AI代理的重要任务。文章还介绍了记忆（Memories）在情境管理中的应用，如Reflexion和生成型代理（Generative Agents）等技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）中的上下文管理问题及其相关技术、隐私和信任问题

不同观点：
• [lend000] 认为当前LLM在上下文管理方面存在瓶颈，尤其是长期对话中的表现不佳。他们建议通过修改Transformer架构来改善这一点，而不是依赖外部方法管理上下文。
• [ares623] 对文章中淡化LLM产生幻觉（hallucination）问题表示不满，并将此问题与加密货币的第二层解决方案相比较，暗示这些技术可能存在类似的缺陷。
• [sgt101] 对LLM的整体机制持怀疑态度，认为其基于概率映射的机制本质上是不稳定的，一个token的变化可能导致完全不同的结果，从而使系统不可靠。
• [AvAn12] 关注隐私和数据保护问题，质疑将更多具体信息上传到技术公司是否安全，并指出这些公司过往在隐私保护方面的记录不佳，且对专有数据有强烈需求。
• [jes5199] 认为当前对LLM技术的应用还只是冰山一角，未来可能会有更复杂的结构被发现和应用，暗示当前的理解和实践仍有很大发展空间。
• [dmezzetti] 强调检索/搜索功能是上下文管理的基础，认为如果输入质量差，输出也会差，并指出搜索问题远未解决。
• [azaras] 分享了使用GitHub Copilot Agent的记忆库模式来管理上下文的经验，但认为这种方式浪费了大量token。
• [truth_seeker] 对上下文工程和提示工程进行了比较，认为在长远来看，提示工程可能比上下文工程更优，因为后者复杂且需要维护，且在人类语言层面仍处于较低水平。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是LLM的上下文管理能力是否可以通过修改架构来显著改善，还是需要依赖外部方法。
• 另一个争议点是隐私和数据安全问题，即是否应该信任大型科技公司处理和管理用户的上下文数据。
• 对LLM技术未来发展潜力的看法也不尽相同，有人持怀疑态度，有人则认为仍有大量未被发现的可能性。

44432596.article_content:
Lance Martin
TL;DR
Agents need context to perform tasks. Context engineering is the art and science of filling the context window with just the right information at each step of an agent’s trajectory. In this post, I group context engineering into a few common strategies seen across many popular agents today.
Context Engineering
As Andrej Karpathy puts it, LLMs are like a
new kind of operating system
. The LLM is like the CPU and its
context window
is like the RAM, serving as the model’s working memory. Just like RAM, the LLM context window has limited
capacity
to handle various sources of context. And just as an operating system curates what fits into a CPU’s RAM, “context engineering” plays a similar role.
Karpathy summarizes this well
:
[Context engineering is the] ”…delicate art and science of filling the context window with just the right information for the next step.”
What are the types of context that we need to manage when building LLM applications? Context engineering is an
umbrella
that applies across a few different context types:
Instructions
– prompts, memories, few‑shot examples, tool descriptions, etc
Knowledge
– facts, memories, etc
Tools
– feedback from tool calls
Context Engineering for Agents
This year, interest in
agents
has grown tremendously as LLMs get better at
reasoning
and
tool calling
.
Agents
interleave
LLM invocations and tool calls
, often for
long-running tasks
.
However, long-running tasks and accumulating feedback from tool calls mean that agents often utilize a large number of tokens. This can cause numerous problems: it can
exceed the size of the context window
, balloon cost / latency, or degrade agent performance. Drew Breunig
nicely outlined
a number of specific ways that longer context can cause perform problems, including:
Context Poisoning: When a hallucination makes it into the context
Context Distraction: When the context overwhelms the training
Context Confusion: When superfluous context influences the response
Context Clash: When parts of the context disagree
With this in mind,
Cognition
called out the importance of context engineering:
“Context engineering” … is effectively the #1 job of engineers building AI agents.
Anthropic
also laid it out clearly:
Agents often engage in conversations spanning hundreds of turns, requiring careful context management strategies.
So, how are people tackling this challenge today? I group approaches into 4 buckets —
write, select, compress, and isolate —
and give some examples of each one below.
Write Context
Writing context means saving it outside the context window to help an agent perform a task.
Scratchpads
When humans solve tasks, we take notes and remember things for future, related tasks. Agents are also gaining these capabilities! Note-taking via a “
scratchpad
” is one approach to persist information while an agent is performing a task. The central idea is to save information outside of the context window so that it’s available to the agent.
Anthropic’s multi-agent researcher
illustrates a clear example of this:
The LeadResearcher begins by thinking through the approach and saving its plan to Memory to persist the context, since if the context window exceeds 200,000 tokens it will be truncated and it is important to retain the plan.
Scratchpads can be implemented in a few different ways. They can be a
tool call
that simply
writes to a file
. It could also just be a field in a runtime
state object
that persists during the session. In either case, scratchpads let agents save useful information to help them accomplish a task.
Memories
Scratchpads help agents solve a task within a given session, but sometimes agents benefit from remembering things across
many
sessions.
Reflexion
introduced the idea of reflection following each agent turn and re-using these self-generated memories.
Generative Agents
created memories synthesized periodically from collections of past agent feedback.
These concepts made their way into popular products like
ChatGPT
,
Cursor
, and
Windsurf
, which all have mechanisms to auto-generate long-term memories based on user-agent interactions.
Select Context
Selecting context means pulling it into the context window to help an agent perform a task.
Scratchpad
The mechanism for selecting context from a scratchpad depends upon how the scratchpad is implemented. If it’s a
tool
, then an agent can simply read it by making a tool call. If it’s part of the agent’s runtime state, then the developer can choose what parts of state to expose to an agent each step. This provides a fine-grained level of control for exposing scratchpad context to the LLM at later turns.
Memories
If agents have the ability to save memories, they also need the ability to select memories relevant to the task they are performing. This can be useful for a few reasons. Agents might select few-shot examples (
episodic
memories
) for examples of desired behavior, instructions (
procedural
memories
) to steer behavior, or facts (
semantic

• [truth_seeker] 对上下文工程和提示工程进行了比较，认为在长远来看，提示工程可能比上下文工程更优，因为后者复杂且需要维护，且在人类语言层面仍处于较低水平。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是LLM的上下文管理能力是否可以通过修改架构来显著改善，还是需要依赖外部方法。
• 另一个争议点是隐私和数据安全问题，即是否应该信任大型科技公司处理和管理用户的上下文数据。
• 对LLM技术未来发展潜力的看法也不尽相同，有人持怀疑态度，有人则认为仍有大量未被发现的可能性。

data.title: The Rise of Whatever
data.author: cratermoon
data.article_summary: 这篇文章最初标题为“怀念电脑带来乐趣的时代”，但作者在写作过程中发现，电脑变得不再有趣的背后有一个黑暗原因，与近年历史中的一系列事件有关。文章回顾了2000年代通过互联网转账的唯一可行选择——PayPal，它控制了资金的使用规则，甚至可以冻结账户并扣留资金长达半年。2010年左右，比特币出现，看似能解决这些问题，实现自由转账，但最终并未实现预期。比特币没有成为广泛使用的货币，而演变成一个充满骗局的生态系统，主要用于投机。PayPal仍然是转账的主要方式，其他平台如Stripe、Patreon、Itch和Ko-fi等也都依赖PayPal或Stripe。作者认为，比特币的失败在于大多数参与者并不关心它作为货币的功能，只关心其价格上涨带来的财富，这种投机文化导致比特币及其衍生品（如NFT）失去了最初的意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对现代技术（如LLMs、自动化工具）及其对学习、创造和行业影响的多种看法和争议

不同观点：
• **gyomu**：担心现代自动化工具（如LLMs）对初学者的负面影响，尤其是这些工具可能让初学者跳过练习和学习过程，直接获得结果，从而破坏学习的“良性循环”。例子包括通过AI生成图片或音乐，而不需要经过长期练习。

• **chrismorgan**：对代码编辑器中自动补全功能的不满，认为这种功能不仅没有提高效率，反而增加了麻烦。虽然理论上可以保持代码语法有效，但在实践中并不实用。

• **Almondsetat**：认为计算机本质上无所谓有趣或无聊，用户的体验取决于他们如何利用计算机。对文章中将支付方式和社交网络与计算机无趣直接关联表示不认同。

• **moritzwarhier**：反对文章中对比特币成为主流货币的期望，认为比特币是一个骗局，并批判将公共资金投入比特币的倡导者。

• **dalemhurley**：分享了对PayPal进入澳大利亚市场时的困惑，以及对PayPal试图通过游说改变银行业务系统的批评。

• **resonious**：同意文章中的许多观点，但不同意对未来的悲观 outlook。认为尽管存在愚蠢和贪婪，但现代技术的成就依然值得肯定，并认为LLMs有其价值，只是需要有效使用。

• **icameron**：感慨过去通过努力和毅力解决复杂脚本问题的技能被LLMs取代，表达了对依赖LLMs生成代码的不满。

• **Arch-TK**：认为LLMs在编程中的流行是因为它们擅长解决重复性问题，而不是因为它们在解决新问题上有多优秀。强调了架构和独特问题解决在产品中的核心价值。

• **Al-Khwarizmi**：部分同意文章观点，但对LLMs持不同看法。认为文章写得很好，但LLMs有其应用价值，尤其是在有效使用的情况下。

• **ZYbCRq22HbJ2y7**：认为文章是对现代平台和流行文化的抱怨，但同时指出LLMs将推动人们意识到以前未注意到的事物，并预期未来信息普及对社会的积极影响。

• **washmyelbows**：同意对现代网络平台的批评，但对LLMs在软件开发中的实用性持肯定态度，认为它们在某些任务中可以节省时间。

• **dwedge**：不喜欢文章中的抱怨语气，认为这是一种常见的“受害者”式写作风格，对文章的幽默和字体选择等表示不满。

• **rednafi**：认为编程一直是在寻找更简单的方法来完成任务，LLMs是这一进程的自然延伸。不认为自动化工具的普及是损失，反而是一种进步。

• **marcus_holmes**：同意结论，但认为LLMs帮助人们认识到过程比结果更重要，强调了创造性活动的内在价值和享受过程的意义。

补充讨论：
- **LLMs对初学者和学习过程的影响**：多个评论提到了LLMs对初学者学习曲线的影响，有人认为这会破坏学习过程，也有人认为这可以解放人们去关注过程而非结果。
- **对自动化工具的不同态度**：一些评论者对自动化工具（如代码编辑器的自动补全功能和LLMs）持批评态度，认为这些工具增加了不必要的复杂性，而另一些人则认为这些工具提高了效率，是技术进步的体现。
- **比特币和经济系统的争议**：对将比特币视为未来货币的期望存在较大争议，部分评论者认为这是不切实际的，甚至是危险的。
- **对文章语气和风格的评价**：部分评论者对文章的写作风格和语气提出了批评，认为其带有抱怨和受害者心态，而另一些人则欣赏文章的写作质量和思考深度。

44461208.article_content:
This was originally titled “I miss when computers were fun”.  But in the course of writing it, I discovered that there is a
reason
computers became less fun, a dark thread woven through a number of events in recent history.
Let me back up a bit.
Bitcoin
Back in the 00’s, if you wanted to move money between arbitrary people over the Internet, you realistically had one option: PayPal.
Either that, or live in some futuristic utopia like the EU where banks consider "send money to people" to be core functionality.  But here in the good ol' U S of A, where material progress requires significant amounts of kicking and screaming, you had PayPal.
The thing about PayPal is that it holds onto your money, but it isn’t a bank?  I do not fully appreciate the architecture or its implications here, but PayPal’s point of view seems to have always been that they can do whatever they want.  They’ve always been pretty fussy about the use of PayPal to facilitate commissioning artists for drawings of unicorn wieners, for example, so if they thought you were doing that, they would just lock your account and also keep all your money for six months.  For safekeeping, I guess.  And interest.
Yet PayPal was the only option for many rinky-dink individuals selling one-off goods and services, so there was some amount of frustration that the
only available middleman
had exclusive right to say how you were allowed to spend your money, or what kind of indie business you were allowed to run.  And if they caught you ignoring the rules then they got to keep your money for half a year.
And then in 2010 or so, I heard about Bitcoin.  And it sounded like the wave of the future.  Finally, a way to just
send money to someone
.  What a fucking concept.  And imagine what you could build with such a system!  Websites could have real tip jars.  Browsers could have tipping built right in that transfer only a few cents, since transactions would be so effortless.
I downloaded a miner (well,
the
miner at the time, I think) and ran it for like a day and failed to mine a coin.  There was nothing else to really do, so I closed it and forgot all about Bitcoin.
Fast forward a bit, Bitcoin has reached mainstream awareness, and…  none of that stuff happened.  Bitcoin is not so much a currency as it is an entire
ecosystem
of schemes.  The only mention I’ve heard in the last year of being able to actually
buy
anything with Bitcoin was gray market estradiol.  (Even gray market
FIP
medication just takes credit cards!)  The only browser with built-in tipping is the one spearheaded by a man whose other claims to fame are inventing JavaScript and wanting to outlaw my marriage, and the token it uses apparently had 80 whole sellers in the past 24 hours.  Sounds like all of that is going great.
Meanwhile, fifteen years later, the state of the art in sending arbitrary people money seems to be…  uh, PayPal.  But now we have Stripe, too, which can take credit card payments if you know how to make a website that uses it, but which
also
forbids drawings of unicorn wieners.  Patreon?  Stripe and PayPal.  Itch?  Stripe and PayPal.  Ko-fi?  Stripe and PayPal.  Nothing is fundamentally different.
But the dream has died.  It almost came true, and then it was immediately co-opted by a bunch of get-rich-quick grifters and a bunch of turbo-libertarians whose entire identities are defined by the Things that they Own and who want to cryptographically impose that on everyone else too because they’re mad that World of Warcraft nerfed warlock or something.
And I suspect the core problem that has wended its way through the history of cryptocurrency is that the vast majority of people involved
do not actually care
what the thing they’re flocking to is.  What they care about is that it has a graph, and that they get rich if the graph goes up, so they say whatever might make the graph go up.  The graph even looks exactly the same for every coin and
NFT
and Whatever else: x-axis time, y-axis dollars.  The only place the
thing
appears at all is in the title, where you can safely ignore it.
Plenty of people will talk up the supposed benefits of their pet thingamajig, of course, but my suspicion is that many of them don’t actually care that much.  They have a
vested interest
in getting other people to buy into the thing, Whatever the thing may be, because then graph go up.
And so you have what I can only call a culture of
Whatever
.  Bitcoin failed as a currency because the people who got most invested in it
do not care
about currency — it could be bottled dragon farts for all they care, except that putting it on the computer means there’s no need to actually worry about a product.  It’s just something to pump the value of; the underlying asset could be, well, Whatever.  And Bitcoin itself is open source, so you can copy it and make your very own coin, your very own Whatever.  With NFTs, you can make an entire
family
of “collectible” Whatevers — a strange descriptor given that you can’t actually c

data.title: LooksMapping
data.author: elsewhen
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由walzr.com制作的互动地图，通过分析数百万Google Maps餐厅评价及评价者的头像照片，利用AI模型为每位评价者的吸引力打分（满分10分）。地图用红色表示吸引力高的餐厅，蓝色表示吸引力低的餐厅。文章承认该方法存在偏见和缺陷，但指出人们经常根据顾客的外貌评判餐厅，而这个网站只是将这种表面判断量化，反映出人们的集体虚荣心。地图目前可在纽约、洛杉矶和旧金山使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基于顾客外貌对餐厅进行评级的现象及其技术与社会影响

不同观点：
• **支持与兴趣**：一些用户如donatj和1GZ0对这种基于现代技术的老派网络恶搞表示支持和兴趣，认为尽管前提有些偏离常规，但背后的技术实现值得赞赏。

• **质疑与反对**：部分用户如pimlottc和d--b对该评级方式表示反感，认为基于外貌的评级不仅无意义，还可能带有偏见和歧视，特别是当某些地区如哈莱姆的餐厅评分普遍偏低时。

• **技术探讨**：getcrunk和bemmu等用户关注该项目的技术实现，包括如何进行数据抓取及人工智能的应用，讨论了这种技术在其他领域的潜在用途，如分类和筛选。

• **社会与文化影响**：Eduard和Mashimo指出该评级系统可能存在对种族和年龄的偏见，例如对黑人或亚裔顾客的打分较低，或对某些种族聚集区的餐厅评分不公。

• **幽默与娱乐**：有些用户如TheLockranore和esafak以幽默的角度看待这个项目，将其比作90年代的浪漫喜剧或建议在纽约应改为热狗摊评级。

补充讨论：
• **媒体报道**：ChrisArchitect提到《纽约时报》曾对该现象进行报道，并将此项目与更广泛的社会讨论联系起来。

• **争议焦点**：该项目引发的最大争议在于其潜在的社会偏见和伦理问题，特别是当评级结果可能反映或强化现有的刻板印象和歧视时。

44461015.article_content:
See Which Restaurants Have The Most Attractive Diners –
According to AI!
Search
I scraped millions of Google Maps restaurant reviews, and gave each reviewer's profile picture to an AI model that rates how hot they are out of 10. This map shows how attractive each restaurant's clientele is. Red means hot, blue means not.
The model is certainly biased. It's certainly flawed. But we judge places by the people who go there. We always have. And
are we not also flawed?
This website just puts reductive numbers on the superficial calculations we make every day. A mirror held up to our collective vanity.

data.title: Electronic Arts Leadership Are Out of Their Goddamned Minds
data.author: dotmanish
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Electronic Arts（EA）在开发《Battlefield》新作时的不切实际目标。尽管此前《Battlefield 2042》表现不佳，EA高层仍设定新作达到1亿玩家的目标，甚至超过该系列自2002年以来总共8800万的销量。为实现这一目标，EA计划推出免费大逃杀模式，投入4亿美元预算（已超支），并关闭原开发工作室，将单人战役外包给其他三个工作室。作者批评EA高层的妄想和不当管理，称其为"商业死亡崇拜"。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏行业的开发成本、商业模式、玩家社区体验以及大公司（如EA）的策略问题

不同观点：
• **游戏开发成本与成功的关系**：
  - joegibbs指出，许多热门游戏（如Fortnite、Minecraft、Ark）最初并非以制作大规模成功游戏为目标，而是在小规模预算下意外走红。他认为，游戏公司应考虑多制作中小成本游戏，测试市场反应后再集中资源。
  
• **对EA及大公司策略的批评**：
  - Qahlel认为，大公司如EA（特别是在Battlefield 2042中）偏离了系列核心玩法，追逐潮流（如Fortnite风格游戏），忽视了增强自身优势。他特别提到，现代游戏的匹配大厅系统削弱了玩家间的互动和社区感。
  - voidfunc直接批评EA管理层过度追求高利润项目和订阅收入模式，认为他们不关注玩家真正需求。
  
• **对公司某些积极举措的认可**：
  - turbofreak赞扬EA发布了《命令与征服》的源代码，并表达了对更多经典游戏源代码发布的期待。
  
• **对高成本游戏成功可能性的质疑**：
  - Nathanba认为，设定高目标并没有错，问题在于执行不力。他认为文章试图引发愤怒，但并未成功。
  - rekenaut质疑高成本游戏是否真的需要如此庞大的用户群，并提出是否应该转而瞄准较小的用户群以降低成本。
  
• **对公司关闭服务器和微交易的批评**：
  - bdcravens提到EA曾因未达盈利目标而关闭了一个拥有数千万年收入的游戏，显示出公司对小规模但盈利项目的短视。
  - vivzkestrel批评EA和育碧等公司将单人游戏强制在线、转向开放世界模式、关闭服务器且缺乏替代方案、以及过度使用微交易。

补充讨论：
• **关于游戏类型和市场趋势的讨论**：
  - joegibbs提到大逃杀类型游戏（如PUBG、Fortnite、Warzone）已经流行一段时间，可能即将过时，类似于之前的开放世界生存游戏和MMO游戏。
  
• **对文章本身的评价**：
  - zombot认为该帖内容过于内部化，外行人难以理解。
  - stodor89认为EA等公司已经多年表现失常，这并不新鲜。
  - superconduct123认为该帖内容贫乏，像是博客垃圾邮件。

争议焦点：
• 大公司是否应继续追逐高成本、高风险的项目，还是应专注于中小成本游戏并观察市场反应。
• 现代游戏的匹配大厅系统是否削弱了玩家间的互动和社区感。
• 高成本游戏的成功是否真的需要极大规模的用户群支持。

Electronic Arts Leadership Are Out Of Their Goddamned Minds
The delusion is absolute
By
Luke Plunkett

I was browsing through some early-morning gaming news today when, after seeing mention of the latest entry in the
Battlefield
series, I nearly spat my cup of tea all over the keyboard.
In a story titled '
What’s wrong with AAA games? The development of the next Battlefield has answers
' on Ars Technica, I read the most
astounding
paragraph:
While [Battlefield]
2042
struggled, competitors
Call of Duty
and
Fortnite
were posting astonishing player and revenue numbers, thanks in large part to the popularity of their Battle Royale modes.
EA's executive leadership believed Battlefield had the potential to stand toe-to-toe with them, if the right calls were made and enough was invested.
A lofty player target was set for Glacier: 100 million players over a set period of time that included post-launch.
From the release of the first
Battlefield
game in 2002 through to the release of
Battlefield 2042
, the series had sold a total of 88 million copies. Total. That's counting
Battlefield 2
,
Vietnam
,
2142
,
Hardline
,
1
,
V
, all of them.
And Electronic Arts executives, living in the same world we're all living in, working in the same video game industry that is falling apart in large part
through their own malpractice
, look at those numbers, look at the performance of the last
Battlefield
game and want this one to have
100 million players
?
To try to meet that goal,
the Ars report says
EA will be releasing a free-to-play Battle Royale mode, have brought in a ton of extra developers, set a budget of $400 million and have now...blown way past that, while also shuttering the studio that
had
been tasked with developing the next
Battlefield's
singleplayer campaign, work that has now had to be farmed out to three
other
studios.
This is a commercial death cult.

data.title: Sound Chip, whisper me your secrets [video]
data.author: rasz
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Giulio Zapparoli在Gulaschprogrammiernacht 23活动上的演讲内容。他分享了自己在业余时间通过使用Arduino Mega和推测方法，对老旧数字音频芯片（如合成器和游戏机中的芯片）进行逆向工程的经验。他解释了如何通过逻辑分析仪等工具，探索芯片内部的算法和压缩方案，并成功构建了这些芯片的模拟器以保存和再现它们的功能。他还提到此次演讲是此前38C3演讲的延续，但更专注于DSP（数字信号处理器）的逆向工程，尤其是那些未被文档记录的芯片。通过探查和分析，他在不破坏原始芯片的情况下，准确地模拟了这些处理器的行为。

Gulaschprogrammiernacht 23
Sound Chip, whisper me your secrets!
giulioz
ZKM Vortragssaal
Hardware and Making
Playlists:
'gpn23' videos starting here
/
audio
57 min
2025-06-19
2025-06-20
438
Fahrplan
Vintage sound chips make cool music, but what's hiding inside of them? Which algorithms are they using?
In the past years I've been dedicating my free time to building emulators for old digital sound chips from synthesizers/game consoles, in an effort to preserve them and make them usable without the original hardware. During this time I went through lots of interesting stuff: silicon reverse engineering, logic analyzers, weird compression schemes, forgotten audio algorithms and more. In this talk I want to share with you what I learned from this process and what's next. Specifically, I will explain how I'm currently reverse engineering a custom DSP from the 90s just by using an Arduino Mega and lots of speculation, and how you can probably apply the same process to other chips as well.
This talk is kind of a sequel for my previous 38C3 talk "Proprietary ICs and dubious marketing claims - let's fight these with a microscope!", where I reverse engineered an old Roland digital piano from silicon die shots, since it was using some custom algorithms no one knew about.
Instead of analyzing fixed behavior hardware, this time I want to focus more on DSPs: processors that can execute code to manipulate audio data in real-time. Since some of them are not documented, the bytecode for their programs will look like random binary without a datasheet.
Instead of going through the silicon directly, I was able to figure out a lot about them just by probing them, building a pretty accurate emulator without destroying the original chip.

data.title: Nintendo locked down the Switch 2's USB-C port and broke third-party docking
data.author: snvzz
data.article_summary: 任天堂在其新推出的Switch 2主机上通过USB-C端口实施了加密保护，故意限制了第三方扩展坞的兼容性。根据《The Verge》的报道，任天堂使用了一种专有的加密方案和可能的专用加密芯片，使得Switch 2无法像其他支持USB-C视频输出的设备那样与第三方 dock 正常通信。作者使用USB-C PD分析器测试发现，Switch 2在与dock进行电力协商时，使用了专有的信息交换协议，导致许多第三方dock无法正常工作。目前，市场上几乎没有兼容Switch 2的便携式dock，即便是以兼容性著称的Jsaux也暂停了相关产品的开发。唯一例外是Antank S3 Max (SiWiQU TV Dock Station)，它能够与Switch 2正常通信。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：任天堂Switch 2的兼容性和潜在的法律问题，特别是涉及充电和视频输出的加密限制，以及是否违反欧盟的相关法规。

不同观点：
• [throwaway7679] 认为，任天堂故意通过破坏兼容性来对待消费者，可能违反了欧盟的无线电设备指令（EU Radio Equipment Directive），特别是拒绝从某些设备接收电力。该评论还引用了一个外部链接（Hacker News的讨论）来佐证任天堂一贯的不良行为。

• [flowerthoughts] 指出，任天堂故意破坏Switch 2与一些配件的兼容性，引入了新的加密方案和专用加密芯片。该评论强调，如果是视频的DRM（数字版权管理）且在商店中明确标注，或许可以接受，但不接受充电方面的限制。该评论还希望USB-IF（USB标准化组织）和欧盟能够对此行为进行惩罚，并认为不应该在USB-C接口上做不尊重互操作性的行为。

• [mrheosuper] 表示不理解任天堂如何能够逃脱这么多对消费者不利的行为，甚至认为任天堂比苹果更糟糕。

• [thih9] 提出，欧盟可能会质疑这种行为，或者将其视为反竞争行为，并询问这种行为是否在欧盟存在，以及其合法性是否已经在欧盟被讨论过。

• [leakycap] 则从市场角度出发，质疑任天堂Switch 2的目标客户是谁，并推测可能是父母为孩子购买或者成年人为自己购买，认为任天堂在设计上的选择并没有很好地满足这两类市场的需求。

补充讨论：
• [snvzz] 提供了一个存档链接，可能指向与讨论相关的更多信息，但链接内容未详细展开。

争议焦点：
1. 任天堂Switch 2的兼容性问题是否构成对消费者权益的侵害。
2. 任天堂使用USB-C接口但不完全兼容所有设备充电功能的行为是否违反了欧盟的法律或行业标准。
3. 是否应该由USB-IF或欧盟对此类行为进行惩罚或规制。

整体来看，评论者普遍对任天堂在Switch 2上的兼容性决策持批评态度，并关注其潜在的法律和市场影响。

Report
How Nintendo locked down the Switch 2’s USB-C port and broke third-party docking
﻿We whipped out a USB-C PD analyzer to test how Nintendo walled its garden this time around.
﻿We whipped out a USB-C PD analyzer to test how Nintendo walled its garden this time around.
by
Sean Hollister
Jul 2, 2025, 7:47 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission.
See our ethics statement.
Photo: Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge
Sean Hollister
is a senior editor and founding member of The Verge who covers gadgets, games, and toys. He spent 15 years editing the likes of CNET, Gizmodo, and Engadget.
There’s always a reason why universal USB-C ports don’t “just work” like you’d expect. In the early days,
it was incompetence
or naiveté. Later, manufacturers often cheaped out. But in the case of
Nintendo’s Switch 2
, it appears to be intentional.
With the Nintendo Switch 2, it should be easy to plug your new, more expensive console into video glasses or TVs when you’re traveling away from home. USB-C makes it so. But Nintendo has intentionally broken the Switch 2’s compatibility with those devices, using a new encryption scheme and some form of dedicated encryption chip, two accessory manufacturers tell
The Verge
.
I haven’t yet found proof of that encryption chip myself — but when I analyzed the USB-C PD traffic with a Power-Z tester, I could clearly see the new Nintendo Switch not behaving like a good USB citizen should.
A third-party Switch dock, plugged into a USB-C PD tester, about to be plugged into the Switch 2. Please forgive the terrible photo.
Photo: Sean Hollister / The Verge
If you’ve been wondering why there are basically no portable Switch 2 docks on the market, this is the reason. Even Jsaux,
the company that built its reputation by beating the Steam Deck dock to market
, tells us it’s paused its plans to build a Switch 2 dock because of Nintendo’s actions. It’s not simply because the Switch 2 now requires more voltage,
as was previously reported
; it’s that Nintendo has made things even more difficult this generation.
How docking works
That “U” in USB isn’t always “universal,” but this is generally true: if you plug any USB-C to HDMI adapter, dock, or hub into a USB-C laptop, tablet or handheld that supports USB-C video output, you can expect to see your screen automatically appear on your TV.
The magic is normally possible because of a simple, standardized set of instructions that any manufacturer can follow to make their docking station or hub “talk” to the computer. In fact, they’re so simple I can mock up a basic version for you right here:
Dock:
“Hi, I’m a power supply. Here are the five different kinds of power I can give you!”
Computer:
“I’ll take 15 volts at 3 amps, thanks!”
Dock:
“Okay, I’m now powering you, you’re no longer powering me, got it?”
Computer:
“Yep! So what are you, anyhow?”
Dock:
“I’m a USB-C PD dock with extra modes, wanna know more?”
Computer
: “Sure.”
Dock:
“I support DisplayPort-Alt mode if you want to output video.”
Computer:
“Go for it.”
Dock:
“Doing it… done!”
This conversation, using standardized (known as “structured”) messages over the USB-C PD protocol, takes a tiny fraction of a second.
But as you probably now suspect, the Nintendo Switch 2 doesn’t do it that way. When you plug the Switch 2 into a third-party dock or hub, it may refuse to negotiate power. Other times, it’ll get the power it asks for, but then the conversation will abruptly grind to a halt.
Because that’s when the Nintendo Switch 2 will start talking in code — proprietary messages only Nintendo can decipher.
By now, you might be wondering how I can see any of this, coded or not. But all you need is a middleman to sniff the USB-C Power Delivery traffic passing between a dock and Nintendo’s handheld, like the
Power-Z KM003C
that I bought for this story. I plug one end of it into the Switch 2 (and other computers to compare), another end of it into the Switch 2’s dock (and other docks to compare), connect its
third
port to my Windows PC with a long cable, then fire up its app to log the passing data.
How the conversation between the Switch 2 and Switch 2 dock begins.
Screenshot: Sean Hollister / The Verge
When I analyze the conversation between the Nintendo Switch 2 and its dock, I can see the two devices begin speaking in Nintendo’s own flavor of “vendor defined” language early in the conversation, before they sign off on any video output. And then, seemingly before the dock confirms that it’s engaged video-out, they send over 30 proprietary “unstructured” messages to one another.
Other USB-C hubs and docks I’ve tested don’t have that same conversation — with one notable exception.
The dock that worked
As of today, precious few third-party docks claim to be compatible with the Nintendo Switch 2. And you probably won’t be surprised to hear that when I tested
the $36 Antank S3 Max
(aka
SiWiQU TV Dock Station
), I found it speaks Nintendo’s coded language

data.title: Serial SPI RAM Emulation on Raspberry Pi Pico RP2040 MCU
data.author: transpute
data.article_summary: 该项目实现了在RP2040（如Raspberry Pi Pico）上模拟SPI RAM的功能，类似于23LC512芯片。它支持READ (0x03)、WRITE (0x02)和FAST READ (0x0B)命令，并在顺序模式下运行，操作不能超出RAM边界。该项目仅支持SPI模式，最大时钟速度取决于系统时钟和操作类型。项目包含四个主要文件（sram.c、sram.h、sram.pio、sram_memmap.ld），通过将这些文件集成到自己的项目中，可以实现自定义内存映射，并预留64KB内存区域用于RAM模拟。配置引脚和PIO等资源后，通过调用`setup_simulated_sram()`启动模拟RAM。为满足严格的时序要求，RAM模拟必须独占使用Core1，并尽可能使用PIO和DMA处理数据传输。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：STM32H7 系列使用 SPI 从模式的性能和实现方式

不同观点：
• Neywiny 认为使用 STM32H7 系列（如 H7A3）的硬件 SPI 从模式是更好的解决方案，无需借助 PIO（可编程IO）。他指出，H7A3 在数据手册中标明可以支持 45 MHz 的全双工 SPI 通信，并且通过超频，实际速度可能更高（如 SPI 读取速度提升 3 倍，写入速度提升近 5 倍）。因此，他认为直接使用硬件 SPI 从模式能带来显著的性能提升。

• Neywiny 提到，虽然需要在软件上做些工作以确保 DMA（直接内存访问）在空闲周期内运行，但这相比性能提升是值得的 tradeoff。他质疑现有方案是否需要占用一个核心来满足延迟需求，认为这可能是一种资源浪费。

补充讨论：
• Neywiny 认为现有方案可能过度依赖 PIO 编程，而忽视了 STM32H7 系列硬件本身支持的高速 SPI 功能，从而导致性能未能充分释放。
• 他还提到，如果能在读命令时正确配置 DMA，可以避免让一个核心专门处理延迟需求，从而释放更多计算资源。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应更多依赖 STM32H7 的硬件 SPI 从模式功能，而非通过 PIO 来实现 SPI 通信。Neywiny 认为硬件方案更高效，尤其是在性能和资源利用方面，而现有方案可能因为 PIO 和核心占用导致资源浪费。

Simulated SPI RAM on RP2040
An SPI RAM implementation for RP2040.
This project allows the RP2040 to act as if it were an serial SPI RAM, similar to a
23LC512
.
The commands READ (0x03), WRITE (0x02) and FAST READ (0x0B) are implented.  The RAM operates in sequential mode, and operations must not go beyond the end of the RAM.
Only SPI mode is supported (no DSPI/QSPI).
The maximum clock rate supported depends on the system clock speed and the operation:
Operation
Max speed
Max speed at 125MHz SYS clock
READ
SYS clock / 10
12.5 MHz
READ (aligned)
SYS clock / 8
15.6 MHz
FAST READ
SYS clock / 8
15.6 MHz
WRITE
SYS clock / 6
20.8 MHz
A READ is considered to be aligned if the start address is a multiple of 4.  There is no requirement for the length of an aligned read to be a multiple of 4 bytes.
Command details
The SPI slave works in SPI mode 0 or 3 - data is transferred in both directions on the rising edge of SCK.  All and addresses are transferred MSB first.
READ
A read command is the byte 0x03 followed by a 16-bit address, MSB first.  Data transfer begins immediately with no delay cycles.  There is no limit to the length of the read, except that it may not go beyond the end of the RAM.  The read is terminated by stopping the SCK and raising CS.
FAST READ
A fast read command is the byte 0x0B followed by a 16-bit address, MSB first.  There are then 8 delay cycles (one dummy byte transfer) before data transfer begins.  Otherwise it is the same as a READ, except it might work at a faster clock rate.
WRITE
A write command is the byte 0x02 followed by a 16-bit address, MSB first.  The data to be written to that address follows immediately.  There is no limit to the length of the write, except that it may not go beyond the end of the RAM.  The read is terminated by stopping the SCK and raising CS.
Using in your own project
It is easiest to integrate by copying the 4 files beginning sram from this project into your project.  Alternatively, you could include this project as a submodule.
You will need to include the
sram.c
file in your source files, and add
pico_generate_pio_header(${NAME} ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/sram.pio)
set_target_properties(${NAME} PROPERTIES PICO_TARGET_LINKER_SCRIPT ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/sram_memmap.ld)
pico_add_link_depend(${NAME} ${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/sram_memmap.ld)
to your CMakeLists.txt to use a custom memory map that reserves the 64kB memory region for the RAM.
Configure the pins, and if necessary DMA channels and PIO SMs by editing
sram.h
.
Start the RAM by including
sram.h
and calling
setup_simulated_sram()
.  This sets up the PIOs and launches the handler on core1.
Note that in order to meet the strict timing requirements, the RAM simulation must have dedicated use of core1, and it uses most of the PIO instructions on both PIOs, though there are still a few instructions spare.
How it works
To meet the tight timing as much is done with PIO and DMA as possible.  There are separate PIO programs handling data in and data out.  The basic flow is:
Both PIOs wait for CS to go low
The read PIO reads the first byte and sends it up to core1, which does the appropriate setup for the command while the address is being received
The read PIO reads all but the last 2 bits of the address.  This is handled on core1 or DMA directly, depending on the command.
The read PIO reads the last 2 bits of the address.  This is handled on core1 or ignored, depending on the command.  Simultaneously the write PIO branches depending on the value of the last 2 bits so that it can discard the right amount of data from the first 32-bit word for unaligned READ comands.
Data is then transferred in or out by the appropriate PIO.
All processing on the CPU is handled by core1, interrupts are not used so there is no overhead going into and out of interrupt contexts, instead the core is always waiting for what it is expecting to happen next. • Neywiny 认为使用 STM32H7 系列（如 H7A3）的硬件 SPI 从模式是更好的解决方案，无需借助 PIO（可编程IO）。他指出，H7A3 在数据手册中标明可以支持 45 MHz 的全双工 SPI 通信，并且通过超频，实际速度可能更高（如 SPI 读取速度提升 3 倍，写入速度提升近 5 倍）。因此，他认为直接使用硬件 SPI 从模式能带来显著的性能提升。

• Neywiny 提到，虽然需要在软件上做些工作以确保 DMA（直接内存访问）在空闲周期内运行，但这相比性能提升是值得的 tradeoff。他质疑现有方案是否需要占用一个核心来满足延迟需求，认为这可能是一种资源浪费。

补充讨论：
• Neywiny 认为现有方案可能过度依赖 PIO 编程，而忽视了 STM32H7 系列硬件本身支持的高速 SPI 功能，从而导致性能未能充分释放。
• 他还提到，如果能在读命令时正确配置 DMA，可以避免让一个核心专门处理延迟需求，从而释放更多计算资源。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于是否应更多依赖 STM32H7 的硬件 SPI 从模式功能，而非通过 PIO 来实现 SPI 通信。Neywiny 认为硬件方案更高效，尤其是在性能和资源利用方面，而现有方案可能因为 PIO 和核心占用导致资源浪费。

data.title: Has Xbox Considered Laying One Person Off Instead of Thousands?
data.author: dotmanish
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了Xbox近期大规模裁员的事件，指出被裁员工并非公司失败决策的负责人。自2013年以来，微软在Xbox品牌上犯下了一系列战略错误，如命名混乱、Game Pass策略失误等，导致公司业绩下滑并进行多轮裁员。作者质疑，为何真正做出这些错误决策的高管，如CEO菲尔·斯宾塞，没有被裁，反而继续领取高额薪酬。文章认为，如果微软希望纠正过去的错误，应该考虑从高层入手，而不是仅裁减基层员工。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GamePass的商业合理性以及公司责任和失败的责任归属问题

不同观点：
• [throwaway638637] 对GamePass的商业模式表示不解，认为其在经济上不合理。他没有详细阐述原因，但暗示对这种商业模式的盈利能力感到困惑。

• [not_your_vase] 认为公司员工对公司或项目的失败负有责任，并提出质疑：为什么员工可以在社会正义问题上发表意见或抗议，但在公司出现问题时却保持沉默。他提出，员工受雇来创造价值，而不是破坏，因此如果项目失败，他们也有责任，而不能仅仅将责任归咎于某一个人。

• [rekabis] 并没有直接讨论GamePass的商业模式，而是通过支持文章的观点表达了对某些“寄生阶层”（Parasite Class）在失败中依然获得高额补偿的不满。他讽刺那些在职业生涯中因 incompetence（无能）而获得奖励的人，暗示对某些公司高管或行业精英在失败中获利的现象感到不满。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是公司失败的责任归属问题。[not_your_vase] 认为员工在公司失败时也应承担责任，而不仅仅是将成功归功于团队，失败则归咎于个人。这涉及公司内部责任分配的公平性和员工在公司治理中的角色。

• [rekabis] 的评论引入了对“失败中的奖励”现象的批评，特别是针对那些在职业生涯中因 incompetence 而获得高额回报的人。这与[not_your_vase] 的讨论有一定的关联，因为两者都涉及失败的责任和后果，但[rekabis] 更关注于公司高层或精英阶层的不当获利问题。

• 总体来看，讨论从GamePass的商业合理性延伸到了公司责任、失败的责任归属以及职场中的不公正现象。

Video Games
Has Xbox Considered Laying One Person Off Instead Of Thousands
None of the people being laid off were responsible for the decisions that have led to these layoffs
By
Luke Plunkett
5:00 PM EDT on July 2, 2025
Share on Bluesky
Share on X (formerly Twitter)
Share on Reddit
Share on Email
SGF 2025
22
Comments
News today that Xbox has
cancelled multiple projects
and
laid off hundreds of workers
, on top of
thousands more let go in earlier layoffs over the last 18 months
, has shaken an industry already pretty damn shaken after
everything that's happened over the last 3-4 years
. This leaves me asking the same question
I've found myself asking a lot lately
: why are the people most responsible for the company's failures not the ones facing the consequences for them?
Microsoft has stepped on rake after rake in the decade since the launch of the Xbox One. I could make a list here of every mistake the company has made--from first-party development mishaps to confusing naming practices to Game Pass' undercutting of an entire industry to more recent stuff like devaluing the brand's identity itself--but you know all this already. You can take your pick as to what you think has been the biggest contributor to a once-dominant console now appearing to be in terminal decline.
Whichever you choose, in whatever order and priority, they've all got one thing in common: they're all strategic mistakes. Everything Microsoft has fucked up since 2013 has come from the very top.
Those fuck ups have consistently pointed the company on a downwards trajectory, to the point where we are now looking at a
fourth
round of layoffs since 2024. Workers who have poured their lives into making games, or marketing games, or making sure studios are run properly, have been cast aside.
None of those people were responsible for calling it the Xbox Series X But Also Series S. The person answering phones at Arkane didn't bet the farm on Game Pass becoming the next Netflix then...not becoming the next Netflix. An artist paid to draw spaceships for a
Halo
game didn't decide that Xbox should mean an actual Xbox but also kinda mean an Oculus Quest 3 and some handhelds and cloud services but also not really.
Xbox executives made those decisions! They've all been bad decisions, one after another, for over a decade now, and as you cast your eyes over the lists of people being affected by these layoffs--their careers and entire lives upended in an instant--that list does not include CEO Phil Spencer.
He remains in his role,
wants to be there for a while yet
, and will remain receiving total compensation in the
millions
, pay that should in theory be a result of the scale of responsibility he is entrusted with. Getting paid millions while you're doing well makes sense! Continuing to be paid millions while your business sucks so badly you think you need to lay off workers because of your terrible decisions, or decisions you're responsible for, makes
no
sense.
If Microsoft really wants to reverse a decade of mistakes, and feels the best way to achieve that is to let someone go, maybe they need to be looking at laying off the people--or person--ultimately responsible for those mistakes.

data.title: The Zen of Quakerism (2016)
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了贵格会（Quakerism）与禅宗（Zen Buddhism）的共通之处，以及作者在这两种精神实践中的个人体验。作者出生于贵格会家庭，从小参加贵格会的静默礼拜，但一直觉得静坐困难。后来在27岁时接触到佛教，通过禅修技巧学会了如何更好地静坐，并从中获得内心的平静。禅宗强调通过冥想觉悟真实本性，而贵格会则通过集体的静默礼拜寻求和平与共识决策。两者都旨在通过释放自我、减轻痛苦来实现精神转化。作者认为，这两种传统都提供了减轻痛苦、追求和平的途径，尽管方法不同，但最终目标相似。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Quakerism的实践、特点及其与其他传统（如禅宗）的比较

不同观点：
• **Quakerism的核心特点**：
  - **quacked**：Quakerism教导对未得权威的不尊重，同时不反对权威本身。其历史实践包括拒绝向国王脱帽致敬和拒绝在作证前按圣经宣誓，强调始终如一地讲真话。
  - **hansonkd**：Quaker崇拜的目的是打开心扉去“倾听”，与以正念为核心的冥想有所不同。Quaker崇拜是在社区中进行，而禅宗冥想常独自面对墙壁。

• **Quakerism的现状与挑战**：
  - **hansonkd**：现代美国Quaker社区，特别是加州，数量稀少且老龄化严重，年轻成员稀缺。无信条和反结构的特点使得新成员难以融入，导致成员流失。
  - **mekoka**：Quakerism应被视为基督教神秘主义的一个分支，可以与其他神秘主义传统（如禅宗、道教、苏菲派等）相提并论，但其知名度不高。

• **Quakerism的品牌与误解**：
  - **hansonkd**：Quakerism面临“品牌问题”，常被误认为是贵格燕麦或阿米什教派，而禅宗更具潮流和神秘感。
  - **monkeycantype**：亲身参与Quaker会议后，发现其与基于圣经的教会更为相似，而非原先预期的对圣文本的怀疑态度。

• **个人经历与外部视角**：
  - **hermitcrab**：作为一名无神论者，尊重Quaker对重要运动和组织的创始贡献，如国际特赦组织、乐施会和绿色和平组织。
  - **kmoser**：基于在Quaker学校的经历，从未感受到在会议中发言需具备“精神深度”的压力，发言完全是自愿且自由的。

补充讨论：
• **Quakerism与其他传统的比较与联系**：
  - **jonaustin**：文章未提及Quakerism和佛教在尊重自然方面的相似性，这是一个值得注意的平行点。
  - **antithesizer**：Buddhism不如Quakerism那样“禅”。

• **对Quakerism的陌生感与误解**：
  - **yapyap** & **_benton**：许多人对Quakerism缺乏了解，误以为与电子游戏或燕麦品牌有关，显示出对Quakerism的认知不足。

• **Quaker会议中的实践建议**：
  - **gandalfian**：在Quaker会议中，若感到沉默过久，可以借助书籍或安静的活动，如乐高，特别是对儿童而言。

争议焦点：
• Quakerism的品牌认知和传播问题，以及它与其他宗教或冥想实践的异同，是讨论中的一个主要争议点。有些人认为Quakerism应被更多地认可为一种神秘主义传统，而实际上它常被误解或忽视。

44413076.article_content:
The Zen of Quakerism
February 1, 2016
By
Peter Taylor
Garden II, ink on paper, by artist and Zen Master Rebecca Nie. View more of her work at rebexart.com.
Q
uakers and Buddhists have a few things in common. Most importantly, they share a common humanity and a commitment to creating peace in the world. They are both enlightenment religions. Both George Fox and the Buddha experienced a transformative, liberating awareness through the dedicated practice of quiet contemplation.
My life is an intersection of these religions. I was born a Quaker, to Quaker parents with Quaker grandparents and great-grandparents. I attended Friends schools through college. I sat in many meetings for worship. I have always been proud to be a Quaker. I found Buddhism later in life, when I was 27 years old. I was looking for a tonic for depression. I found Buddhist philosophy and writing soothing to my condition. I liked that Buddhism talked about meditation as a remedy to suffering.
Even though I had been meditating all of my life in Quaker meetings, I had always struggled with how to do it. As a child, meeting for worship was somewhere between difficult and excruciatingly painful. To amuse myself, I would count things. I would count people with glasses. I would count ceiling tiles. I would count the seconds on my watch. I would welcome any spoken message that would break up the monotony of the silence. I would welcome the break of meeting so I could talk and run around again.
When I learned to meditate in the Buddhist style, I learned to keep my awareness focused by counting my breaths. I learned to hold my body still while I focused my mind. I found a specific place to put my hands. In meditation, I was relieved of the burden of being moved by the Spirit to speak and say something spiritually profound. Learning Buddhist meditation techniques taught me how to sit in Quaker meeting. Through all those years of Quaker upbringing and Quaker education, I had somehow missed that fundamental teaching.
In my Zen practice, I sat many hours of meditation. I did sitting meditation, walking meditation, chanting meditation, bowing meditation, eating meditation, tea-drinking meditation, and listening meditation. I went on a retreat to the Detroit Zen Center and did cooking meditation, cleaning meditation, weeding meditation, and hours and hours of sitting meditation. All that meditation was not necessarily peaceful or easy as I did it. What I found is that the rest of my days became more peaceful and easier to manage. The meditation worked. It created peace.
Besides the regular sitting practice, Zen is based on a philosophy that is different from Quakerism. Zen compelled me to practice with the enticement of an enlightenment experience. The Zen tradition is a long tradition, dating back to the Buddha (who is believed to have lived and taught between the sixth and fourth centuries B.C.E.), of purposefully awakening. Zen masters through the ages have skillfully worked with their disciples and students to create the conditions for awakening to the True Nature of reality. The push of a Zen practice is to recognize your own True Nature. The promise of that liberating experience was compelling enough to inspire me to do all that meditation.
As I studied Zen in Toronto, Ontario, I did not attend Quaker meeting. That changed when my family and I moved back to New Jersey in July 2013. Instead of finding an area Zen
sangha
(practice community), I returned to Quaker meeting for worship.
Upon returning to Quakerism, I found a group of earnest seekers, coming together in silence to try to find peace in their lives and create peace in the world. The meeting drew me into the community by inviting me to be on various committees. Committee work and the business of the meeting is one way that Quakers spread the peace of Sunday meeting for worship into the rest of the week.
In monthly meeting for business, making difficult decisions and resolving conflict test the peace of the worship. As a spiritual practice, recognizing the will of the group and releasing your own opinions can be transformative. It requires patience, respect, faith, and competent leaders to guide the process. When these factors are not present, the group may make decisions, but individuals feel excluded, egos grow, and conflict escalates. I’ve witnessed this in many meetings throughout my life. I’ve also witnessed excellent conflict resolution, where all participants feel committed to the direction of the group and uplifted through the resolution of conflict and a clear way forward.
Recognizing your True Nature in Zen and coming to a decision through Quaker process are both exercises in understanding our egos and, ultimately, easing our suffering by releasing them. This is a transformative experience that Quakerism and Buddhism offer.

  - **hermitcrab**：作为一名无神论者，尊重Quaker对重要运动和组织的创始贡献，如国际特赦组织、乐施会和绿色和平组织。
  - **kmoser**：基于在Quaker学校的经历，从未感受到在会议中发言需具备“精神深度”的压力，发言完全是自愿且自由的。

补充讨论：
• **Quakerism与其他传统的比较与联系**：
  - **jonaustin**：文章未提及Quakerism和佛教在尊重自然方面的相似性，这是一个值得注意的平行点。
  - **antithesizer**：Buddhism不如Quakerism那样“禅”。

• **对Quakerism的陌生感与误解**：
  - **yapyap** & **_benton**：许多人对Quakerism缺乏了解，误以为与电子游戏或燕麦品牌有关，显示出对Quakerism的认知不足。

• **Quaker会议中的实践建议**：
  - **gandalfian**：在Quaker会议中，若感到沉默过久，可以借助书籍或安静的活动，如乐高，特别是对儿童而言。

争议焦点：
• Quakerism的品牌认知和传播问题，以及它与其他宗教或冥想实践的异同，是讨论中的一个主要争议点。有些人认为Quakerism应被更多地认可为一种神秘主义传统，而实际上它常被误解或忽视。

data.title: Next month, saved passwords will no longer be in Microsoft’s Authenticator app
data.author: ColinWright
data.article_summary: 微软将在下个月取消对密码的支持，并推动用户转向使用更为安全的通行密钥（passkeys）。从2025年7月开始，微软Authenticator的自动填充密码功能将停止工作，而到8月，所有保存的密码将无法再使用。用户需要转而使用PIN码、指纹或面部识别等通行密钥进行登录。通行密钥使用公钥加密技术，存储在个人设备上，而非服务器上，能有效防止网络钓鱼和暴力破解攻击。如果用户仍想使用密码，可以将其保存在微软Edge浏览器中，但专家建议利用此次机会转向使用通行密钥。要设置通行密钥，用户需打开Authenticator应用，选择账户并设置通行密钥。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软推动passkeys引发的各种技术与安全性讨论

不同观点：
• **支持passkeys的观点**：
  - sedatk认为微软此举是大胆且必要的，尽管passkeys的实施存在不一致和恢复流程不完善的问题，但微软作为大公司带头推动密码less认证，可能会促使其他公司采用这种方法。
  
• **反对passkeys的观点**：
  - dontTREATonme表示passkeys在多设备使用时非常混乱，不同设备上的passkey无法清晰区分，导致登录失败，最终选择放弃使用。
  - RHSeeger指出passkeys无法满足其与家人共享密码、多设备登录、以及防止设备损坏导致账户丢失的需求，认为密码管理器如1Password或Bitwarden更适合。
  - joeblubaugh认为对于大多数用户来说，passkeys增加了不必要的复杂性，且在设备损坏或丢失时更容易导致账户无法访问。
  - cycomanic质疑passkeys的安全性，认为过去强调的双因素认证（2FA）更为安全，而现在passkeys似乎只依赖单一因素。

• **对微软动机质疑的观点**：
  - execat质疑微软强推passkeys的动机，认为此举激怒了很多用户，背后可能有其他目的。
  - jeroenhd则认为文章夸大了微软强迫用户使用passkeys的情况，实际上只需安装Edge浏览器即可解决大部分问题。

• **对技术细节和实施不满的观点**：
  - mzajc担心passkeys的“供应商认证”问题会导致用户选择受限，质疑微软是否以用户利益为出发点。
  - djrj477dhsnv强调如果无法将私钥导出到自己的备份解决方案，则不会考虑使用passkeys。
  - yodon分享了在更换iPhone后，微软账户在Microsoft Authenticator中失效的经历，表示不再信任微软管理passkeys。

• **对浏览器和应用选择的讨论**：
  - withinrafael简要解释了微软Authenticator应用将停止密码自动填充功能，并会在特定时间后删除存储的密码。
  - wkat4242强烈反对使用Edge浏览器，认为其体验糟糕，且多数网站不支持passkeys，因此选择自托管解决方案。
  - simonw作为iPhone和Mac用户，对文章内容感到困惑，不确定是否需要采取行动，并对Microsoft Authenticator应用与Windows功能的名称混淆提出疑问。

补充讨论：
- 用户对passkeys的理解和接受度普遍较低，主要因为技术复杂性和跨设备使用不便。
- 微软推动passkeys的过程中，沟通和实施细节引发了不少用户的不满和质疑。
- 争议焦点在于passkeys的多设备管理复杂性和安全性，以及微软是否通过此举推广其Edge浏览器。

44426985.article_content:
Tech
Microsoft Is Erasing Your Passwords Next Month. Do This ASAP
Authenticator's autofill feature will stop working this month, but the biggest change is one month away.
Dashia Milden
Editor
Dashia is the consumer insights editor for CNET. She specializes in data-driven analysis and news at the intersection of tech, personal finance and consumer sentiment. Dashia investigates economic shifts and everyday challenges to help readers make well-informed decisions, and she covers a range of topics, including technology, security, energy and money. Dashia graduated from the University of South Carolina with a bachelor's degree in journalism. She loves baking, teaching spinning and spending time with her family.
See full bio
Dashia Milden
July 2, 2025  10:30 a.m. PT
3 min read
You'll still be able to access your passwords, but Microsoft's new approach is a safer way to log into your accounts.
Andriy Onufriyenko/Getty Images
Starting this month, you'll no longer be able to use Microsoft Authenticator's autofill password function, a move the company is making to transition from passwords to passkeys. Last month, Microsoft stopped letting you save new passwords in the app.
Next month is the biggest change, all your saved passwords will no longer be in the Authenticator app. You'll have to use passkeys instead -- such as a PIN, fingerprint or facial recognition.
Attila Tomaschek, CNET's software senior writer and digital security expert, believes passkeys are a safer alternative to the risky password habits that 49% of US adults have, according to a
recent CNET survey
.
"Passwords can be cracked, whereas passkeys need both the public and the locally stored private key to authenticate users, which can help mitigate risks like falling victim to phishing and brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks," said Tomaschek.
Using the same password for several accounts or adding personal hints can be a convenient way to remember your login. But it's a big risk for scammers, identity theft and fraud. Here's more on Microsoft's plan for eliminating passwords and how to make the switch to passkeys before August.
Microsoft Authenticator will stop supporting passwords
Microsoft Authenticator houses your passwords and lets you sign into all of your Microsoft accounts using a PIN, facial recognition such as Windows Hello, or other biometric data, like a fingerprint. Authenticator can be used in other ways, such as verifying you're logging in if you forgot your password, or using two-factor authentication as an extra layer of security for your Microsoft accounts.
In June, Microsoft stopped letting users add passwords to Authenticator, but here's a timeline of other changes you can expect, according to
Microsoft
.
July
2025:
You won't be able to use the autofill password function.
August
2025:
You'll no longer be able to use saved passwords.
If you still want to use passwords instead of passkeys, you can store them in Microsoft Edge. However, CNET experts recommend adopting passkeys during this transition.
"Passkeys use public key cryptography to authenticate users, rather than relying on users themselves creating their own (often weak or reused) passwords to access their online accounts," said Tomaschek.
Why passkeys are a better alternative to passwords
So what exactly is a passkey? It's a credential created by the Fast Identity Online Alliance that uses biometric data or a PIN to verify your identity and access your account. Think about using your fingerprint or Face ID to log into your account. That's generally safer than using a password that is easy to guess or susceptible to a phishing attack.
Passkeys aren't stored on servers like passwords. Instead, they're stored only on your personal device. More conveniently, this takes the guesswork out of remembering your passwords and the need for a
password manager
.
How to set up a passkey in Microsoft Authenticator
Microsoft said in a
May 1 blog post
that it will automatically detect the best passkey to set up and make that your default sign-in option. "If you have a password and 'one-time code' set up on your account, we'll prompt you to sign in with your one-time code instead of your password. After you're signed in, you'll be prompted to enroll a passkey. Then the next time you sign in, you'll be prompted to sign in with your passkey," according to the blog post.
To set up a new passkey, open your Authenticator app on your phone. Tap on your account and select "Set up a passkey." You'll be prompted to log in with your existing credentials. After you're logged in, you can set up the passkey.

data.title: What to build instead of AI agents
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI代理的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• [mccoyb] 认为构建代理是有趣的，但当前的“上下文工程”存在问题，需要新的思路来解决。他强调了代理在任务中缺乏有效过滤机制的问题，并提出了通过用户交互动态构建程序和模型的可能性。他认为通过测试套件引导代理是一种强大的强化机制，并期待代理在软技能方面的进展。

• [mindwok] 对AI代理的大规模应用持怀疑态度，更喜欢紧密控制AI的行为，以提供个人的品味和方向。他认为赋予AI更多自主权并不一定可取，因为这样会失去与AI的连接。

• [transcriptase] 对只有1-2年经验的技术权威表示质疑，暗指对AI代理的讨论可能过于超前或炒作。

• [rm999] 认为如果有明确的解决方案，就不需要代理。他指出，编程问题通常有明确的解决方案，使用代理会增加不必要的复杂性。不过，在聊天助手等场景中，代理确实能提供价值，因为这些场景的解决方案空间不明确。

• [joeblubaugh] 批评许多代理的例子只是为了更快地发送垃圾信息，质疑其真正价值。

• [ilaksh] 认为在使用最先进的LLM时，代理的优势显现出来，特别是在需要AI参与的任务中。他预计未来会有更多基于代理的计算机使用趋势，并认为这些代理将具备更好的记忆系统和学习能力。

• [JSR_FDED] 通过实践发现代理不如使用更简单的模式可靠，感觉代理技术仍处于不成熟的阶段。

• [btown] 认为许多问题可以通过更具体的提示和工具描述来解决，并质疑文章中缺乏实际使用的例子。他相信更多的工作可以受益于代理编排。

• [jlaneve] 和 [intellectronica] 都提到将LLM集成到传统的工作流编排工具中，可以更容易地构建和实现价值。他们强调使用AI来完成只有AI能完成的任务，而不是过度依赖代理。

• [bravesoul2] 质疑是否需要以对话方式使用LLM，建议直接向用户提供明确的上下文信息，并构建无幻觉的系统。

• [abelanger] 指出代理的稳定性依赖于其组件的质量，并强调需要接近100%的成功率或内置纠正机制。

• [deadbabe] 认为AI代理只是快速构建服务的临时工具，最终会被更便宜的硬编码功能取代。

• [dmezzetti] 认为文章忽略了一个更重要的点：许多问题仍然可以通过传统的编码来解决。

• [aryehof] 认为确定性的业务流程不适合LLM编排，呼应了文章中的发现。

补充讨论：
- 代理的可靠性和稳定性是争议的焦点，特别是其组件质量和成功率的问题。
- 讨论中还涉及到代理的实际应用场景，如聊天助手和复杂交互任务，这些场景中代理的价值更明显。
- 一些评论者强调了简化解决方案的重要性，质疑过度依赖代理的必要性。
- 对未来AI代理的发展趋势和技术进步有不同预测，特别是在记忆系统和自动化方面的潜力。

data.author: tysone
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：会议的低效及替代方案（如AI笔记工具）的讨论

不同观点：
• meros认为会议的信息密度低，主要目的是为了让中层管理人员感觉良好，并通过口头指示来维护其权威，而不是通过书面备忘录。这与写作能力不足有关。
• jawns指出，管理层可能认为员工逃避会议是在偷懒，而实际上员工是为了在满足不切实际的会议出席要求的同时完成实际工作。
• nlawalker表示，很多会议实际上是展示，应该以异步方式进行，但历史惯例要求所有人参加 live 活动。
• mlsu认为，很多人不喜欢阅读和写作，这使得通过书面沟通变得困难，必须找到与这些同事有效沟通的方法。
• captainkrtek对AI笔记工具在面试中的应用持怀疑态度，认为生成的笔记过多且有错误，最终还是需要自己写总结。

data.author: edent

data.comments_summary:

44461976.article_content:
Your Exit Strategy Dream Is My Customer Nightmare
Published on:
2025-07-04 07:40:00
by
Stefano Marinelli
6 min read
Photo by Ilias Gainutdinov on Unsplash
I've  always been a believer in human relationships. Whenever possible, I  always prioritize direct dialogue. I've never been a fan of abstractions  when it comes to relationships.
Just  like in the IT world, I am convinced that you can usually solve much  more with a direct conversation than with a thousand intermediate steps.  Too many layers, even if theoretically sound, just complicate things.
And  this is one of the reasons I've always tried, as much as possible, to  avoid overcomplicating the relationship with my clients. It's why I have  always sought, as much as possible, to engage with businesses where I  can speak with people, not "offices" or "departments".
Take
the example of the roof repairs on my house
: I spoke with the people  who did the work. They did an excellent job and even fixed things I  hadn't mentioned because, in their words, "a satisfied customer is a  customer who will call back". A few days earlier, "large, structured"  companies had sent completely different quotes without even looking at  our roof. "The people we send will assess it then, but we'll instruct  them to do what's in the quote". It was schematic, inflexible. Probably  efficient from their point of view, but not from mine. Replaceable by  AI? Of course: X square meters of roof, Y job, Z per square meter ->  cost is â¬W. Without anyone truly caring about what my roof might  actually need.
For  this very reason, I dislike talking to salespeople. It's one thing when  I'm buying a product (with verifiable features, etc.), but it's  different when I'm buying a service or a consultation. Salespeople do  their job, which is to sell. And they try to sell what they don't have,  what they don't know, and what I don't need. The better they are, the  more they sell me things I don't need. And, frankly, I don't like that  very much.
This  is why I prefer to talk to the person who actually provides the  service. The one who gets their hands "dirty". But many people love to  create a structure, an abstraction. Even when it's not necessary.
A  few days ago, I identified an open-source software solution with two  versions, a "community" and an "enterprise" one, but it still seemed  approachable. I quietly started running some tests and realized that  this solution might be suitable for offering some new services to both  current and new clients. Something new and innovative, yet consistent  with my philosophy. As I often do, I did some research on the company  behind it. I discovered it was a tiny company with extremely low  revenue - so low that my contribution could, at least in part, help it  grow. Not because my business would be huge, but because it could  provide visibility in a market where they currently have no presence.  Noticing how few people were in the company, I decided to contact the  dev/founder/CEO directly.
A  human connection, to understand the project's direction, to see if it  was the right fit for my needs, and to potentially fund the development  of features I was interested in. I would also explain that, given the  cost and my trust in the product, I would use the "enterprise" licenses  for my clients, bringing further revenue to their business.
As  I often do in these cases, I proceeded on two fronts: I opened a  support ticket asking about the status of support for a specific  operating system, and I sent a private message to the dev/founder/CEO on  one of the platforms where the company is active, briefly explaining my  idea.
After  a few minutes, the private message was declined (I'm not even sure if  it was read), and the ticket received a terse reply, something like  "that OS is not officially supported". Period. They didn't even get to  the next part, the one where I would have funded development and  provided my clients with the enterprise version.
This  kind of shutdown is disheartening. Of  course, not every startup thinks this way, and the search for a  scalable business model is perfectly legitimate. But when exponential  growth becomes the only metric for success, the value of the customer and the product gets lost in the process.
It's not the first time, and in  different forms, I notice a fairly common pattern nowadays: a certain  market just isn't of interest. They want massive clients - or they'd  rather shut down the project. It's not a mindset of "hey, I have an idea  and I want to build it", but rather "how can I make mountains of money  in a short time? Let me find an idea that might work". Why does everyone  dream of being the multi-million-dollar startup with a product that  "disrupts the market", while giving up on a healthy, organic, clean path  of gradual growth?
Itâs as if success has been reduced to a single metric: financial gain, where the ultimate satisfaction is purely economic. Betraying your own principles - or the trus

主要讨论点：关于虎鲸（Orca）的行为、名称及其引发的不同看法

不同观点：
• [robaato的观点] 认为文章有趣，提到虎鲸使用海带茎相互按摩，并将其行为与海豚的表演性行为作比较，带有些许调侃意味。
• [bmitc的观点] 认为文章标题应将“Killer whales”改为“Orcas”，强调对虎鲸的称呼问题，认为“Killer whales”具有误导性。
• [metalman的观点] 分享虎鲸分享食物的行为，特别提到野生虎鲸会主动向人类投掷食物，表现出与人类互动的倾向，并附上相关链接支持其观点。
• [fuzzfactor的观点] 以幽默方式回应虎鲸相互梳理的行为，提问“如果它们不这么做，谁来做？”，带有调侃性质。
• [wiether的观点] 作为英语非母语者，对“killer whales”这一名称感到不适，认为“whales”在科学分类上不准确，“killer”则可能引发不必要的恐惧。

补充讨论：
• 名称争议：多位评论者（bmitc和wiether）提到“killer whales”这个名称的问题，bmitc建议改为“Orcas”，wiether则从语言和情感角度分析名称的不适，反映出对虎鲸命名和分类的关注。
• 虎鲸行为：metalman强调虎鲸分享食物和主动与人类互动的行为，提供了额外信息和链接，显示出对虎鲸社会行为和智力的兴趣。robaato则调侃虎鲸行为类似于海豚的表演性行为，表现出对动物行为的不同解读。
• 争议焦点：评论中对虎鲸名称的争议是讨论的核心，尤其是其科学性和名称带来的潜在情感影响。

主要讨论点：关于艺术作品的修复、时间错误、艺术归属及其影响、以及画作内容的趣味发现

不同观点：
• [fumeux_fume] 认为《最后的晚餐》也是用油画颜料绘制的湿壁画，并指出该画很快 deteriorated，需要不断修复。这暗示了某些著名画作在技术上的局限性和维护难度。

• [doodlebugging] 关注文章中提到的时间错误，指出 restoration 在开始之前就已经完成，认为这是一个编辑错误，暗示日期数字可能被误输入或交换，质疑文本的准确性。

• [alpineman] 质疑“发现”一词的使用，认为既然艺术品早已存在，用“发现”可能不准确。同时提出是否知道作品由拉斐尔亲自绘制会产生影响，并进一步思考这种影响是否应该存在。

• [ludicrousdispla] 以幽默方式指出画作中出现恐龙这一趣味元素，属于对画作内容的轻松、非学术性观察。

• [ZiiS] 对艺术家助手未能学会油画表示怀疑，指出即使是高水平助手，学习油画（通常认为比湿壁画简单）似乎不应成为难题，质疑这些助手的技术能力。

补充讨论：
- 时间错误的争议是讨论中的一个焦点，[doodlebugging] 提出了明显的年代错误，暗示文本编辑可能存在问题。
- [alpineman] 提出的归属问题引发了关于艺术作品归属是否应影响其价值和认知的思考。
- [ZiiS] 的评论引发了对艺术技法难易程度以及历史背景下艺术家助手能力的讨论。

data.author: greyblake
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Rust中如何解决同一trait不能有多个重叠的blanket implementation的限制问题。具体场景是在开发Joydb时遇到了Adapter trait的两种实现：UnifiedAdapter和PartitionedAdapter，希望用户只需实现其中一个即可自动获得Adapter trait的功能，但由于Rust的限制无法直接实现。

解决方案是使用标记结构体（marker structs）和关联类型（associated types）来绕过这一限制。具体步骤包括：

1. 定义标记结构体Unified<A>和Partitioned<A>，这些结构体仅用于类型级别的分发。
2. 定义一个辅助trait BlanketAdapter，并分别为Unified<A>和Partitioned<A>实现这个trait。
3. 修改Adapter trait，增加一个关联类型Target，以委托给正确的BlanketAdapter实现。

通过这种方法，成功解决了Rust中不能有重叠blanket implementation的问题，使得用户只需实现UnifiedAdapter或PartitionedAdapter，即可自动获得Adapter trait的功能。

Serhii Potapov
July 01, 2025
#
rust
#
traits
#
patterns
Rust's trait system is famously powerful - and famously strict about avoiding ambiguity.
One such rule is that
you can't have multiple blanket implementations of the same trait
that
could potentially
apply to the same type.
What Is a Blanket Implementation?
A
blanket implementation
is a trait implementation that applies to
any
type meeting certain constraints, typically via generics.
A classic example from the standard library is how
From
and
Into
work together:
impl
<
T, U
>
Into
<
U
>
for
T
where
U
:
From
<
T
>
,
{
fn
into
(
self
)
->
U
{
U
::
from
(
self
)
}
}
Thanks to this, when you implement
From<T>
for
U
, you automatically get
Into<U>
for
T
. Very ergonomic!
The Restriction
However, Rust enforces a key rule:
no two blanket implementations may overlap
- even
in theory
. Consider:
impl
<
T
:
TraitA
>
MyTrait
for
T
{
...
}
impl
<
T
:
TraitB
>
MyTrait
for
T
{
...
}
Even if no type currently implements both
TraitA
and
TraitB
, the compiler will reject this. The reason? Some type
might
satisfy both in the future, and that would make the implementation ambiguous.
A Real-World Problem
While working on
Joydb
, I ran into this exact problem.
I have an
Adapter
trait responsible for persisting data.
In practice, there are two common ways to implement it:
A
unified adapter
that stores all data in a single file (e.g., JSON). In Joydb, this is
UnifiedAdapter
.
A
partitioned adapter
that stores each relation in a separate file (e.g., one CSV per relation), called
PartitionedAdapter
.
Ideally, users would only need to implement one of those and get the
Adapter
trait "for free".
But Rust won't let me define two conflicting blanket implementations. So... is there a workaround? 🤔
The Trait Definitions in Joydb
Here are the relevant traits in Joydb:

how can I let someone implement either

I discovered a solution in
this Rust forum post

The key idea is to use:
Marker structs
like
Unified<T>
and

to wrap adapter types.
A helper trait,
BlanketAdapter

An

in the

data.title: As a Labrador swam by me out to sea his owner said I hope he doesn't meet a seal
data.author: austinallegro
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者与伴侣在大流行前定期下海游泳的经历。一次游泳时，一只叫亚瑟的拉布拉多犬超越了他们，似乎打算游得很远，作者担心它的安全。后来得知，狗主人担心亚瑟遇到海豹，因为这会让他错过电视上的比赛。几个月后，作者看到亚瑟和海豹一起玩耍，像朋友一样互动。大流行期间，作者的家庭新增了一只叫伦尼的拉布拉多犬。带伦尼去海边游泳时，它总是试图把作者赶回岸边，像牧羊犬赶羊一样。虽然游泳过程不太放松，但作者觉得在海上对拉布拉多犬让步是合适的。文章通过人与狗的关系，展现了自然行为与陪伴的乐趣。
